regions.name: Middle East
overview: The US–Iran confrontation stayed at a high tempo without a decisive break. On 21 November Iran fired two waves of drones and ballistic missiles at US-used bases in Bahrain. It was the fourth attempt in about a week; Bahrain reported a fire at a civilian industrial site and two injured. Tanker attacks around Hormuz continued: at least three ships were hit on 21 November, and the IRGC says more tankers struck mines on 24–25 November. Al Jazeera puts Hormuz oil traffic about 40% lower. CENTCOM widened the blockade to ship-to-ship transfers on 19 November. Washington reportedly decided on 23 November to delay any new strike campaign, and Trump said he leans toward resuming strikes after the new year if talks fail. Israel is lobbying for a short, intense campaign, while Qatar, Egypt, Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan try to restart talks.

The Saudi–Houthi war is escalating around the Red Sea. A Houthi missile hit Riyadh's PIF tower on 19 November, the tallest building in the capital. Riyadh then faced near-daily salvos, with three ballistic missiles on 21 November and two more plus a cruise missile on 25 November, and a drone was downed near Jeddah port on 26 November. The coalition struck Hodeidah repeatedly; Houthi media reported 10 dead on 23 November. On 24–25 November it ordered the evacuation of Hodeidah port and hit the port and airport. The Houthis now threaten all Saudi Red Sea ports. Houthi forces remain about 60 km from Aden, which is preparing its defences.

In Gaza, Israel has moved to a campaign against Hamas's internal security apparatus. Strikes killed the director-general of Internal Security, Naim Abu Nahl, on 24 November and the northern Gaza security chief, together with his wife and two daughters, overnight on 24–25 November; a Hamas deputy minister and his wife were killed on 26 November. Al Jazeera counted at least 16 killed in 24 hours. In the West Bank, settler-linked shootings killed men near Ramallah (20–21 November) and east of Bethlehem (23 November). In Israel, Eisenkot's Yashar signed a coalition deal with Yisrael Beytenu and is aiming for a swearing-in around 2 December, although the Democrats froze talks.

The week's most unexpected event was in Libya. On 22 November, Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury in Benghazi port, hit a cargo ship and destroyed a helicopter; about 10 people were injured, including Libyans. This brought the Russia–Ukraine war onto Libyan soil and prompted protests from Tripoli and the AU. Elsewhere, Iraq defused the Jurf al-Sakhar standoff with a compromise and a partial deployment on 19–20 November, but Kataib Hezbollah reportedly still holds the town centre. Israel continued near-daily strikes and demolitions in southern Lebanon and raids in Quneitra and Daraa. Tunisia jailed former truth-commission head Sihem Bensedrine. No new incidents were found in Jordan or Egypt.

countries.name: Gaza
incidents: 24 Nov — Gaza Strip: An Israeli strike killed Naim Abu Nahl, director-general of Hamas's Internal Security Service, according to Hamas and Middle East Eye.

25 Nov — Gaza City (Shati camp): An overnight Israeli air strike on an apartment killed Muhammad Abu al-Awf, director of internal security in northern Gaza, along with his wife and two daughters aged 13 and 15. It was the second killing of a senior Hamas security official in under 24 hours.

26 Nov — Deir al-Balah: An overnight Israeli strike on an apartment building killed Hamas deputy education minister Khaled Abu Nada and his wife, according to Palestinian media; the IDF said it targeted a 'senior' Hamas operative.
26 Nov — Gaza City (Shati camp): Palestinian media reported three people killed in another Israeli strike; Al Jazeera counted at least 16 Palestinians killed across Gaza in 24 hours.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. After launching its first declared ground operation west of the Yellow Line on 18 November, Israel has turned to a decapitation campaign against Hamas's internal security apparatus. This week it killed the service's director-general on 24 November, the northern Gaza security chief with his family on 25 November, and a deputy minister on 26 November. Daily death tolls in the mid-teens are again being reported. These strikes erode Hamas's ability to police the territory and raise the chance of Hamas retaliation. The diplomatic track is weak. Kushner has warned that Israel risks 'global pariah' status, and the Board of Peace accuses the caretaker government of blocking its disarmament plan, while Netanyahu says he cannot advance the plan as caretaker. A new Eisenkot government, possibly from early December, could reopen the plan, but not quickly. Over the next 90 days, expect continued lethal strikes on Hamas commanders and civilians, further land control beyond 60% of the Strip, and a severe winter shelter crisis for about 2.1 million people in tents. The post-ceasefire toll reaching 1,800 by end-January remains likely, as in the open forecast, and a single day with 25 or more killed remains a realistic possibility.

countries.name: Lebanon
incidents: 21 Nov — Braachit (Bint Jbeil district): An Israeli air strike targeted the town, according to Al Jazeera reporting compiled by the CFR conflict tracker; no casualty figures were given.
22 Nov — Majdal Zoun / Qantara: Lebanese state media reported Israeli shelling of Majdal Zoun and demolitions in Qantara.

24 Nov — Qabrikha / Touline / Zawtar al-Sharqiyah / Mayfadoun / Kfar Tebnit: Lebanese media reported a series of Israeli strikes and explosions in the IDF's southern buffer zone, and state media said at least three Israeli drones exploded over southern towns; the IDF calls such activity routine demolition of Hezbollah infrastructure. No casualties were reported.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Israel's posture in the south is unchanged. It occupies a roughly 10 km buffer zone and carries out near-daily air strikes, drone explosions, shelling and demolitions, from Braachit and Majdal Zoun to Qabrikha, Touline and Kfar Tebnit. Katz has stated that the occupation is indefinite. For a second week no deaths were reported, but the 5 November strike that killed three girls and their grandmother shows how quickly lethal incidents recur. The Lebanese state is acting against Hezbollah through the courts, bringing charges and arrest warrants against members over explosives and arms cases, but disarmament still lags the June framework. The key 90-day driver is the US–Iran track. Washington reportedly delayed new strikes on Iran on 23 November, and Trump says he favours resuming after the new year if no deal is reached. A renewed campaign against Iran would make Hezbollah involvement and Israeli strikes on the Dahiyeh and the Bekaa much more likely. Without that trigger, expect continued buffer-zone demolitions, targeted strikes on suspected operatives and arms convoys, US sanctions, and a growing security gap as UNIFIL's mandate ends on 31 December. A strike on the Dahiyeh remains unlikely, as in the open forecast. A single Israeli strike killing three or more people is likely before end-January.

countries.name: Iran
incidents: 21 Nov — Bahrain (Riffa / Awali / Isa / Juffair): Iran launched two waves of drones and ballistic missiles at US-used bases in Bahrain; the IRGC claimed hits on Patriot radars. Bahrain said its air defences intercepted several attacks, but a civilian industrial facility was hit and set on fire, injuring two people. A US official said no US forces were damaged and called it the fourth attempt in about a week.

21 Nov — Sirik (Hormozgan): Explosions and air-defence activity were reported in the southern Iranian town shortly after the Bahrain attacks, according to Iranian accounts; CENTCOM denied an Iranian claim that a surface-to-air missile damaged a US F-16 on 20 Nov.

21 Nov — Strait of Hormuz: At least three tankers were attacked in or near the strait. UKMTO reported two tankers hit by projectiles as they exited the Gulf, with no casualties, and Iran's navy said a third hit a mine east of the strait and caught fire. Reports put the number of tankers hit since 16 Nov at seven.

24–25 Nov — Strait of Hormuz: The IRGC said three tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines on 24 Nov, and two more on 25 Nov, while transiting an 'unauthorized route' despite US escorts. UKMTO did not confirm the mine reports. Al Jazeera estimates Hormuz oil traffic is down about 40%.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The confrontation is at its most intense in more than a year: Trump said on 23 November that Iran had fired more drones and missiles in the past week than at any time in over a year, all intercepted. Iran's 21 November ballistic-missile and drone waves on Bahrain show a willingness to raise the weapon class against US bases. Tanker attacks and claimed mine strikes continue despite US escorts, and CENTCOM widened the blockade to ship-to-ship transfers on 19 November. The hyped tanker convoy to break the blockade from Kharg was walked back by Iranian media. Strategically, Washington reportedly delayed any new campaign by at least a week on 23 November. Trump says the war is funded through January and that he would resume strikes after the new year if no deal is reached, while Israel presses for a short, intense campaign and Britain and Gulf states urge restraint. Qatar, Egypt, Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan are trying to restart talks; a Qatari delegation was in Tehran on 20 November. Over the next 90 days, expect continued tit-for-tat at Hormuz and on Gulf bases, with the largest risk window from January. A US and/or Israeli strike on inland Iran remains a realistic possibility, as in the open forecast, and a Hormuz reopening agreement remains unlikely before February.

forecasts.statement: The United States and/or Israel strike targets on the Iranian mainland away from the Hormuz coast and islands (e.g. Tehran, Isfahan, Natanz, Fordow, or other inland sites).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or Al Jazeera report a US or Israeli strike on a site in an inland Iranian province (not Hormozgan, Bushehr coast or the Gulf islands) between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

forecasts.statement: The United States and Iran publicly announce an agreement or framework to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if both governments, or the mediating state (Qatar/Oman) with both sides confirming, announce an agreed arrangement for reopening Hormuz, as reported by Reuters or AP, by 2027-01-31.

countries.name: Yemen
incidents: 20 Nov — Hodeidah / Sanaa: The Saudi-led coalition carried out a 'special operation' against Houthi smuggling and weapons-transport capabilities at Hodeidah port and struck military targets in Sanaa, including a main supply depot. Houthi media reported a strike on Mokha port.

20 Nov — Marib / al-Jawf / Lahij: Government forces reported six air strikes on Houthi positions north of Marib and clashes in al-Jawf and Lahij; more than 350,000 people have been displaced, with Taiz receiving the most.
23 Nov — Hodeidah: Houthi media reported 10 people killed in a coalition strike that hit a building of the Public Telecommunications Corporation.

25 Nov — Hodeidah: After ordering civilians to evacuate Hodeidah port on 24 Nov, the coalition said it struck Houthi 'operational capabilities' at the port, and Houthi media said the city's airport was also hit. The Houthis threatened all Saudi Red Sea ports, and AFP reported Houthi fighters about 60 km from Aden, where defences are being prepared.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The coalition has shifted from broad strikes toward Hodeidah, the Houthis' main port and supply lifeline. It struck the port and Sanaa depots on 20 November and a telecom building on 23 November (10 dead, per Houthi media). On 24–25 November it ordered the port evacuated and then hit the port and airport, which signals an attempt to choke Houthi imports and weapons flows. The Houthis answered by striking Riyadh's PIF tower and threatening Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports. On the ground, the Houthis hold the Yemeni shore of Bab al-Mandeb and sit about 60 km from Aden. Fighting continues in Lahij, Marib and al-Jawf, and displacement now exceeds 350,000. Over the next 90 days, expect a push toward Jabal Kharaz and Aden's outer defences, and continued coalition strikes on Hodeidah's port, fuel and telecom infrastructure. Expect further disputed mass-casualty incidents and a worsening humanitarian situation as port capacity falls. Houthi control of the strait and threats to Red Sea ports keep an attack on merchant shipping a realistic possibility, as in the open forecast. Breaking the Taiz siege remains unlikely.

forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera or OCHA report that government forces have reopened a road into Taiz city allowing civilian or aid traffic, by 2027-02-12.

forecasts.statement: The Houthis attack (with a missile, drone, uncrewed boat or boarding) a commercial vessel in the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb or Gulf of Aden.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if UKMTO, JMIC, Reuters or AP report an attack on a merchant ship in the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb or Gulf of Aden that is claimed by the Houthis or attributed to them by UKMTO/JMIC or a Western government, between 2026-11-19 and 2027-02-19.

countries.name: Israel
incidents: 21 Nov — Dura al-Qara (near Ramallah, West Bank): Hamza Masoud Salim Abdo, 42, died of gunfire that a Palestinian official attributed to guards of a nearby settlement, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry; the IDF said it was looking into the incident.

23 Nov — al-Rashayida area (east of Bethlehem, West Bank): A Palestinian shepherd was shot dead by a settler, according to official Palestinian sources. The Palestinian civil affairs authority reported about 30 settler attacks in one day, including the torching of some 12 vehicles north of Ramallah.

23 Nov — Tel Aviv / Washington: The US reportedly decided to hold off at least a week on new strikes on Iran despite Israeli pressure, with Netanyahu pushing for a short, intense campaign and Mossad chief Gofman lobbying in Washington the week before.

25 Nov — Jerusalem: Eisenkot's Yashar signed a coalition agreement with Yisrael Beytenu (reportedly giving Liberman's party the Defence ministry) and is aiming for a swearing-in as early as 2 Dec; the Democrats froze talks and UTJ is seeking rabbinic approval to open formal negotiations.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The direct threat to Israeli territory is latent rather than active, since no attacks on Israel were found this week. West Bank violence remains lethal, with settler-linked killings near Ramallah on 20–21 November and east of Bethlehem on 23 November. The Shin Bet identifies more than 700 Jewish Israelis and 115 sites involved, and Chief of Staff Zamir told lawmakers the army lacks the tools to handle it. The main escalation risk is Iran. Israel is pressing for a short, intense campaign, while Washington delayed strikes on 23 November and Trump says he would resume after the new year if no deal is reached. A resumed US/Israeli campaign would very likely bring Iranian missile and drone fire on Israel and move it to CRITICAL. Iranian fire on Israel before late February is a realistic possibility. Politically, Eisenkot has signed Yisrael Beytenu and is aiming to swear in a government around 2 December, but the Democrats froze talks and the Haredi track depends on UTJ's rabbis. A Knesset-approved Eisenkot government by mid-January therefore remains a realistic possibility, as in the open forecast, and a slight upward drift is warranted if UTJ formally joins. Expect continued West Bank raids and settler attacks, isolated Palestinian attacks, and intense coalition bargaining.

countries.name: Iraq
incidents: 19–20 Nov — Jurf al-Sakhar (Babil): After a compromise reached on 19 Nov, Iraqi security forces arrived on 20 Nov. Federal Police are to run a new control headquarters, Energy Police are securing the oil pipeline, and an army brigade, a Federal Police battalion and two PMF brigades will guard pipelines. Kataib Hezbollah is expected to withdraw within a month; PM al-Zaidi said the forces were 'not waging war'.

25 Nov — Jurf al-Sakhar (Babil): Al-Mada, cited by 964media, reported that Kataib Hezbollah still controls the centre of the town and that no government force has entered it, contradicting earlier reports of a full deployment.

25 Nov — Baghdad: Iraq's Federal Supreme Court ruled that Baghdad may deploy federal troops to secure international borders, including in territory administered by the Kurdistan Region; the KRG rejected the orders as unconstitutional.

25 Nov — Al Luhais (south of Baghdad): The National Security Service reported two more oil-smuggling operations, including a tapped pipeline, as the government widened its crackdown on illicit oil networks.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Baghdad avoided a battle at Jurf al-Sakhar through a compromise brokered after Qaani's visit. State forces have arrived and Federal Police are to run a control headquarters, but Kataib Hezbollah reportedly keeps the town centre and has a month to withdraw, and it may try to tie a full exit to the June 2027 disarmament deadline. The first real test is therefore postponed rather than passed. The government is pressing on with its anti-smuggling campaign (Al Luhais on 25 November), and a Federal Supreme Court ruling allowing federal troops on Kurdistan's borders has opened a new Baghdad–Erbil dispute, with Kurdish warnings about confrontation with the Peshmerga. Cross-border drone attacks on Kurdish opposition sites and the 8 November Khor Mor strike show the continuing drone threat in the north, and ISIS cells remain active around Kirkuk. Over the next 90 days, the most likely outcome is a slow, partial Kataib Hezbollah drawdown with symbolic state presence, plus continued friction with Erbil. A resumed US–Iran war from January would make militia attacks on US sites likely; an attack on the US Embassy or Erbil consulate remains unlikely in the base case, as in the open forecast.

forecasts.statement: A drone or rocket attack targets the US Embassy in Baghdad or the US consulate in Erbil.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, Shafaq News or Rudaw report a drone or rocket attack aimed at (including intercepted over) the US Embassy in Baghdad or the US consulate in Erbil between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

forecasts.statement: Iraqi government security forces deploy inside the town of Jurf al-Sakhar (Babil), the Kataib Hezbollah stronghold.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, Shafaq News or Rudaw report that Iraqi army, police or other state forces (excluding PMF units of Kataib Hezbollah itself) have entered and established a presence inside Jurf al-Sakhar town, with or without fighting, by 2027-01-31. A visit by inspection committees alone does not count.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
incidents: 19 Nov — Riyadh (King Abdullah Financial District): A Houthi missile hit the Public Investment Fund tower, blowing out windows across seven to eight floors; Saudi civil defence reported material damage to the tower and nearby buildings and no injuries.

21 Nov — Riyadh: The coalition intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles fired at the capital after eight emergency alerts in 24 hours, the third consecutive day of alerts; a drone aimed at the kingdom's south was destroyed hours later.

25 Nov — Riyadh / Western Region: The coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh and a cruise missile aimed at the Western Region; the Houthis said they targeted Jeddah and Jazan ports in response to strikes on Hodeidah and threatened all Saudi Red Sea ports.

26 Nov — Jeddah / Riyadh: Saudi air defences destroyed a drone near Jeddah Islamic Port overnight, and an explosion was heard over Riyadh around midnight as missiles were downed; coalition spokesman al-Maliki said no civilians were injured by debris.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The Houthi campaign has reached symbolic targets in the capital: the 19 November hit on the PIF tower, Riyadh's tallest building, was the most visible damage so far. Salvos now come almost daily, with civil defence issuing eight alerts in 24 hours on 20–21 November. The Houthis are also widening their target set to Red Sea ports, firing at Jeddah and Jazan on 25 November and downing a drone near Jeddah port on 26 November, in reply to the coalition's Hodeidah port campaign. Saudi authorities count at least 26 killed in the kingdom since 23 September. Over the next 90 days, expect continued missile and drone fire on Riyadh, energy sites (Ras Tanura, Shuqaiq) and Red Sea ports, periodic debris damage and flight disruption, and continued Saudi strikes on Hodeidah and Sanaa. Egyptian and other partners will keep thickening air defences. A single strike killing five or more remains a realistic possibility, as in the open forecast. Damage at Jeddah or Jazan port from a Houthi attack is a realistic possibility by end-January.

forecasts.statement: A single Houthi missile or drone attack on Saudi territory kills five or more people.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Saudi authorities, Reuters, AP or Al Jazeera report at least five deaths from one Houthi attack (including interception debris) on Saudi territory between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

forecasts.statement: A Houthi missile or drone attack (including interception debris) causes damage at Jeddah Islamic Port or Jazan port.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Saudi authorities, the coalition spokesman, Reuters, AP or Al Jazeera report physical damage (to facilities, vessels or cargo) at Jeddah Islamic Port or Jazan port from a Houthi attack between 2026-11-26 and 2027-01-31. Unverified Houthi claims alone do not count.

countries.name: Syria
incidents: 24 Nov — Jubata al-Khashab (northern Quneitra): Israeli troops detained a Syrian civilian during a raid, according to Alikhbaria TV; he was released the next day.
24 Nov — Ain al-Bayda (Quneitra): Israeli forces entered the village and set up a checkpoint to search passersby, according to Syrian state media.
24 Nov — Abidin (Daraa): An Israeli force with seven military vehicles entered the village and searched several homes, according to Anadolu citing Syrian media.

25 Nov (reported) — Quneitra countryside: Israeli forces destroyed farmland and a livestock shelter and blocked farmers from their land, and state media reported Israeli shelling of farmland near al-Mantara Dam, with no casualties.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Israel's presence in the south is entrenched. SANA counted 125 incursions and 55 checkpoints in Quneitra in October alone, and this week saw detentions in Jubata al-Khashab, checkpoints in Ain al-Bayda, a raid into Abidin in Daraa, farmland destruction and shelling near al-Mantara Dam. The Arab League condemned the incursions on 18 November, and Katz says Israel will stay indefinitely. Suwayda remains outside Damascus's control, and the Jaramana car bomb of 14 November and the earlier August bombing show a persistent IED threat around the capital. ISIS remains active in the east. Over the next 90 days, expect continued Israeli raids and detentions with occasional deaths, further IED and ISIS attacks on government forces, and tension tied to Syria's troop commitment in Saudi Arabia. A security agreement with Israel stays unlikely before a new Israeli government settles in. A single ISIS attack killing five or more government personnel is a realistic possibility before late February.

forecasts.statement: A single attack claimed by or attributed to the Islamic State kills at least five Syrian government soldiers or security personnel.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, SANA or SOHR report at least five Syrian government military or security personnel killed in one attack claimed by IS or attributed to IS by Syrian authorities or SOHR between 2026-11-26 and 2027-02-26.

countries.name: Egypt
incidents: 23 Nov — Cairo / Doha / Ankara: Egypt was reported alongside Qatar, Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan as working to restart US–Iran talks, as Washington weighed delaying new strikes on Iran.
25 Nov — Cairo: The Foreign Ministry said it is following up on missing Egyptian nationals after a migrant boat carrying 27 Egyptians sank off Benghazi, Libya (the sinking occurred on 5 Nov).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Egypt itself was quiet this week. Its risks are external and rising. The Houthis now threaten all Saudi Red Sea ports and are firing at Jeddah and Jazan, which brings the war closer to the Red Sea corridor that feeds the Suez Canal, even though canal revenue rebounded 94% year on year in October. Egyptian forces deployed in Saudi Arabia to defend 'sensitive sites' have been labelled a declaration of war by the Houthis, but have not been attacked. Cairo remains a key mediator on Iran and Gaza and a growing security actor in Libya, where migrant deaths off Benghazi and the Ukrainian strike on a Russian warship there add regional instability on its western flank. Over the next 90 days, watch for Houthi attacks on Egyptian personnel or vessels, threats to Suez-bound shipping, Sinai security and pressure on Rafah from Israeli operations in Gaza. HIGH would apply if Egyptian forces are directly attacked, Suez traffic is targeted, or a significant terrorist attack occurs in Egypt.

countries.name: Jordan
countries.coa: HIGH maintained, under review. Searches of Petra, the Jordan Times and wire services found no new security incidents for 19–26 November. The threat picture is still shaped by the Karak church attack on 23 October (nine killed) and the 5 November Amman stabbing of a police corporal, both by recently released militants. The state's response is still unfolding: death sentences for the Karak attackers on 15 November, an updated counter-terrorism strategy introduced on 8 November with legislation pending, and a nationwide Telegram block on 16–17 November. That signals concern about online recruitment and copycat attacks. Over the next 90 days, expect continued raids and arrests, parliamentary action on counter-terrorism laws and release rules, steady drug and weapons smuggling from Syria, and possible Jordanian strikes in southern Syria. A resumed US–Iran war from January would raise the risk to US-used bases in Jordan, and a direct attack would justify CRITICAL. Another fatal terrorist attack remains a realistic possibility, as in the open forecast. If none occurs by mid-December, a downgrade to MODERATE is warranted.

forecasts.statement: Another attack inside Jordan that authorities describe as terrorist kills at least one person.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Jordanian authorities (Public Security Directorate/Petra), as reported by Reuters, AP, The National or Asharq Al-Awsat, attribute a fatal attack on Jordanian territory to terrorism between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

countries.name: Libya
incidents: 22 Nov — Benghazi (port): Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian Black Sea Fleet corvette Merkury (Project 20380) in the port, also striking the cargo ship MV Angara and reportedly destroying a Ka-27 helicopter. Zelenskyy said seven naval drones were used, and Reuters, citing local medical sources, reported about 10 injured, including Russians and Libyans.

23–24 Nov — Tripoli / Benghazi: The Presidential Council vowed military, political and legal measures over the Benghazi incidents, Libya demanded clarification from Kyiv and considered an international lawsuit against Ukraine, and the African Union condemned the attacks on the port.
23 Nov — Tripoli: Presidential Council head Menfi met the 5+5 Joint Military Commission on military unification; the Ports Authority warned that maritime security threats could disrupt supplies.
25 Nov — Ankara: Turkish President Erdogan received Khalifa Haftar on his first official visit to Turkey, as the US reaffirmed support for a Libyan-led, consensus-based political process.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained, with an upward risk. The sinking of the Russian corvette Merkury in Benghazi on 22 November brings the Russia–Ukraine war onto Libyan soil. It exposes Russia's naval and logistics foothold in Haftar's east and puts Libyan port workers and infrastructure at risk; the Ports Authority already warns of supply disruption. Both Libyan camps condemned Kyiv, which is a rare point of unity, while Haftar's first official visit to Ankara on 25 November shows him balancing his Russian ties with closer ties to Turkey. Internally, there were no new armed clashes in Zawiya or Tripoli this week. The 4+4 and 5+5 tracks continue, but the east–west institutional split and Haftar's succession remain unresolved, and a teachers' dispute is building. Over the next 90 days, watch for Russian retaliation or force protection measures in eastern Libya, further Ukrainian attacks on Russian assets, renewed militia fighting west of Tripoli, and disputes over oil revenue. A further attack on Russian military assets in Libya is unlikely but no longer remote, and deadly clashes in Zawiya or Surman remain a realistic possibility, as in the open forecast.

forecasts.statement: Armed clashes between rival groups in Zawiya or Surman kill three or more people in a single episode.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, Libya Observer, Libya Security Monitor or UNSMIL report at least three deaths from one episode of armed clashes in Zawiya or Surman between 2026-11-12 and 2027-02-12.

forecasts.statement: Another drone or missile attack hits a Russian military vessel, aircraft or facility on Libyan territory or in Libyan waters.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, Defense News or Libya Observer report a new attack (after 2026-11-22) striking a Russian military ship, aircraft or base in Libya, whether claimed by Ukraine or attributed by Libyan or Russian authorities, between 2026-11-26 and 2027-02-26.

countries.name: Tunisia
incidents: 20 Nov — Tunis: A court sentenced Sihem Bensedrine, 76, former head of the Truth and Dignity Commission, to five years in prison on corruption charges; ex-commission member Khaled Krichi received four years and ex-minister Mabrouk Korchid six. Amnesty International called the verdict an 'outrageous injustice'.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Tunisia's crisis is political rather than armed. The Bensedrine sentence on 20 November, on top of her 25-year sentence in June, the final convictions in the mass 'conspiracy' trial in September and the October terrorism sentence for journalist Zied el-Heni, shows the judiciary being used systematically against critics. The 17 October protest, the largest against Saied in years, and the October clashes over deaths linked to police show that economic and political grievances can turn into street unrest. The state of emergency runs until 31 December, and parliament is debating the 2027 budget amid claims of recovery. Over the next 90 days, expect further prosecutions of opposition figures, journalists and activists, economically driven protests with a risk of deadly escalation if security forces use more force, and smuggling and migration pressure along the Libyan border. Renewal of the state of emergency is the default expectation.

regions.name: Ukraine/Russia
overview: Russia answered the Kerch Bridge strike with one of the largest attacks of the war. Overnight into 20 November, Zelensky said, Russia fired more than 400 drones and more than 110 missiles, 27 of them ballistic. The strikes hit the Podilskyi, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges in Kyiv, energy, rail and logistics sites, and a hospital in Zaporizhzhia Oblast. At least eight people were killed, six in Kyiv and two in Lviv, and nuclear plants cut output, causing outages in Kyiv and 10 regions. The same night, Russian missiles and a drone entered Polish airspace and crashed, and a 'triple-tap' strike in Kryvyi Rih killed a child and a paramedic.

Ukraine kept up its deep-strike campaign against Russia's oil system. Targets included the Kaleikino pumping station near Almetyevsk in Tatarstan (19 November), an industrial site in Smolensk Oblast (20 November) and the Syzran and Novokuibyshevsk refineries in Samara Oblast (25 November, reported but not officially confirmed). ISW reports that Putin has acknowledged the strikes impose a substantial budget burden. Separately, Murmansk Governor Chibis was arrested on 23 November, the first arrest of a sitting governor since the full-scale invasion. On the ground, ISW recorded no advances by either side on 24 November.

Diplomacy is under time pressure but has produced nothing new. On 24 November Zelensky said US envoys Witkoff and Kushner want a peace deal 'as soon as possible', ideally by January, but not 'at Ukraine's expense alone'. Trump laughed this off, saying he is 'not under a timeline'. Kushner said Russia is open to European involvement in talks on security architecture. The large prisoner exchange agreed in Abu Dhabi on 11 November had still not been reported as carried out by 26 November, beyond the two-to-three-week window first given. Lukashenko offered on 24 November to fly to Moscow with Zelensky, which Kyiv rejects.

Spillover onto the periphery continues below the threshold of hostilities. Moldova recorded 19 drone incursions in November as of 23 November, including crossings on 20, 21 and 23 November, and its parliament ratified a military-technical cooperation pact with Ukraine on 19 November. In Georgia, the president pardoned 232 convicts, only three of them political prisoners, protests reached day 726, and the party-ban hearing was adjourned to 30 November. Armenia published its draft new constitution on 23 November, with Pashinyan vowing to resign if it is rejected, and launched the practical phase of TRIPP with Trump, while opposition factions vow to block the referendum. Azerbaijan pressed on with the closed Karimli trial.

countries.name: Ukraine
incidents: 20 Nov — Kyiv: In what Moscow called retaliation for the Kerch Bridge strike, Russia fired more than 400 drones and more than 110 missiles, 27 of them ballistic, at energy, transport and rail targets, per Zelensky. The Podilskyi, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges were damaged and traffic restricted. At least eight people were killed (six in Kyiv, including three water-facility workers, and two in Lviv) and 28 wounded, per Prime Minister Koretskyi. A hospital in Zaporizhzhia Oblast was also hit, and nuclear plants cut output, causing outages in Kyiv and 10 regions (Al Jazeera).

20 Nov — Kryvyi Rih: In a Russian 'triple-tap' strike, local officials said ballistic missiles hit a restaurant parking lot and drones then struck rescuers at the scene. A seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic were killed (CNN).

24–25 Nov — Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia and Kyiv oblasts: ISW recorded no advances by either side on 24 November and counted 96 Russian drones overnight, 64 of them jet-powered. Overnight into 25 November Russia launched 112 strike drones, of which 88 were neutralised. A drone hit a minibus near Fedorivka in Kharkiv Oblast, killing one and injuring seven, one man was killed in Bila Tserkva district, and much of Zaporizhzhia city and oblast lost power (Ukrainska Pravda, via a Substack digest).

24 Nov — Kyiv: Zelensky told Bloomberg that US envoys Witkoff and Kushner want a peace deal 'as soon as possible', ideally by January, but that peace must not come 'at Ukraine's expense alone'. Trump said on 25 November he is 'not under a timeline' (Ukrainska Pravda, Meduza). The Abu Dhabi prisoner exchange had still not been reported as carried out.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Russia delivered its promised 'painful' response to the Kerch Bridge strike. The 20 November barrage of more than 510 drones and missiles hit three more Kyiv bridges and the grid, killed at least eight people and forced nuclear plants to cut output, and double- and triple-tap strikes on rescuers continue, as in Kryvyi Rih. Over the next 90 days, expect large combined salvos roughly every one to two weeks against power, heating, bridges and rail, with daily jet-drone attacks and heavy glide bombs on front-line towns in Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk, Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts. On the ground the front is largely static: ISW recorded no advances on 24 November, and its 18 November assessment says Russian casualties now exceed recruitment. Full Russian capture of Kostiantynivka before mid-February therefore remains unlikely. On diplomacy, Washington is pushing for a deal by January while Moscow ties any settlement to territory and a new European security order. A general or energy ceasefire within 90 days remains unlikely. A negotiating round that includes Russian, Ukrainian and European delegations is still a realistic possibility before the end of January, since Kushner says Russia accepts European involvement on security architecture, but only there. The Abu Dhabi prisoner exchange has slipped past its window with no public explanation. Watch whether it happens, whether US pressure on Kyiv for concessions grows, and how far the grid degrades as winter sets in.

forecasts.statement: Russian forces take full control of the town of Kostiantynivka (Donetsk Oblast).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if DeepState's map or ISW's assessment shows the whole built-up area of Kostiantynivka under Russian control (a Russian MoD claim alone does not count).

forecasts.statement: A new round of negotiations on ending the war is held in which Russian and Ukrainian delegations both take part (directly or through US-mediated proximity talks) together with an official EU or European-government delegation at the same venue.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or the Kyiv Independent reports that a negotiating session took place with Russian, Ukrainian and EU (or named European government) delegations present at the same talks by that date. Separate bilateral meetings, such as Europeans meeting only Ukraine or the US, do not count.

countries.name: Russia
incidents: 19 Nov — Almetyevsk (Tatarstan): Ukrainian drones attacked oil storage tanks near Almetyevsk. The Tatarstan head's press service confirmed the attack and said a major fire was avoided, while Astra reported the Transneft Kaleikino pumping station, a Druzhba pipeline hub, as the target (Meduza).

20 Nov — Smolensk Oblast: A Ukrainian drone attack damaged an industrial facility, and Russia's Defence Ministry said it intercepted 310 Ukrainian drones. The same night, Russian strikes sent two likely missiles and a drone into Polish airspace, which Poland's defence minister called a provocation (Al Jazeera). Russia's embassy in Warsaw later called Polish protests 'Russophobic'.

23 Nov — Murmansk: Law enforcement arrested Murmansk Oblast Governor Andrei Chibis, which ISW calls the first arrest of a sitting Russian governor since the full-scale invasion. ISW also reports Putin acknowledging that Ukraine's strikes on oil infrastructure impose a substantial financial burden on the budget.

25 Nov — Samara Oblast: Fires broke out overnight at Rosneft's Novokuibyshevsk and Syzran refineries after a drone attack, per Astra and Ukrainska Pravda, but there was no official confirmation that the plants were hit.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Russia is waging an active war and its rear is under sustained attack. Ukraine is hitting the oil system deep inside Russia, at Tatarstan, Smolensk and Samara this week, and Putin now publicly concedes the budget cost. Russia retaliated for the Kerch Bridge with a record-scale salvo, which again spilled into Polish airspace. Over the next 90 days, expect Moscow to engage with Washington's push for a deal by January while holding to its territorial and European-security demands and rejecting an unconditional ceasefire. Expect Ukraine to keep hitting refineries, pumping stations, ports and Crimea supply routes, with more domestic fuel-market measures and airport closures. Full road traffic across the Kerch Bridge before mid-February remains unlikely, and repeated strikes on the rail section have deepened Crimea's reliance on ferries and the land corridor. The Chibis arrest fits a widening campaign of elite and defence-sector arrests and signals tightening control, not instability. The large Abu Dhabi prisoner exchange is overdue against the two-to-three-week window TASS gave and has had no public update. It is still more likely than not before 20 December because all three parties are committed to it, but confidence has fallen. Expect more Russian airspace incidents with NATO neighbours as salvos target western Ukraine. Watch the exchange, US–Russia contacts, and fuel prices and export restrictions.

forecasts.statement: Russia and Ukraine carry out a prisoner exchange in which each side releases at least 500 prisoners of war (in one swap or in stages announced as part of the Abu Dhabi deal).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or the Kyiv Independent reports that at least 500 POWs per side have been exchanged under the agreement by that date, per official Ukrainian or Russian statements.

forecasts.statement: Russia reopens the road section of the Kerch (Crimean) Bridge to general vehicle traffic in at least one direction after the 16–17 November 2026 span collapse.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Russian official channels (Transport Ministry, Grand Service Express or Crimean authorities), as reported by Reuters, AP, the Moscow Times or Meduza, state that ordinary vehicle traffic has resumed across the road bridge by that date. Rail-only traffic, ferries or a temporary pontoon do not count.

countries.name: Belarus
incidents: 24 Nov — Minsk: In an interview with Le Point published on 24 November, Lukashenko proposed that he and Zelensky fly together to Moscow for talks to end the war, offering himself as a guarantor of Zelensky's safety. He said Russian forces were winning 'slowly' and that Russia, Ukraine and Belarus should decide the region's arrangements (Reuters via Belta). Zelensky has rejected going to Moscow and instead invited Lukashenko and Putin to Kyiv.

25 Nov — Minsk: In the same interview, Lukashenko said Belarus would consider removing Russian nuclear weapons from its territory as part of a Ukraine peace settlement, denied knowing in 2022 that Russian troops in Belarus would attack Kyiv, and ruled out his son Nikolai succeeding him (Ukrainska Pravda).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. This was another week without security incidents on Belarusian soil. Lukashenko instead used a Le Point interview to market himself as a mediator, offering to fly to Moscow with Zelensky, and as a bargaining chip, saying he would consider removing Russian nuclear weapons under a peace deal. Kyiv rejects both his mediation and Moscow as a venue. Over the next 90 days, expect Minsk to keep pitching itself as a venue and guarantor while staying firmly aligned with Moscow, and to keep seeking sanctions relief from Washington through prisoner releases, although Envoy Coale's promised return visit is still overdue. Expect continued smuggling-balloon and drone friction with Lithuania and Poland through the winter, more snap readiness inspections and continued repression at home. A rise to HIGH would require direct military coercion of a NATO neighbour, a serious armed border incident or Belarusian forces joining the war.

countries.name: Moldova
incidents: 19 Nov — Chișinău: Parliament ratified, with 56 votes, a five-year military-technical cooperation agreement with Ukraine signed on 26 October, covering expertise sharing, training, technology transfer and joint defence capability (Moldova1).

20 Nov — Ștefan Vodă district: A drone entered Moldovan airspace at 14:48 from Ukraine's Odesa region toward Crocmaz and left a minute later near Tudora, per the Defence Ministry. Separately, a drone crossed from Ukraine near Arioneşti in Dondușeni district and exited about nine minutes later through Briceni district (Moldova Live).

21–23 Nov — Northern and eastern Moldova: A jet-powered drone crossed Moldovan airspace twice on 21 November, and on 23 November an unidentified drone, likely Russian, entered and was lost near the eastern border, likely after returning to Ukraine (Moldova1, ISW). The General Staff counted 19 incursions in November and said Moldova can detect drones but lacks the means to neutralise them.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Incursions are now near-daily, with 19 in November as of 23 November and drones crossing the south-east, the north and, on 17 November, the capital. There are still no casualties, no officially confirmed impacts on Moldovan soil and no evidence of deliberate targeting, so the HIGH threshold is not met. Chișinău's answer is to borrow Ukrainian know-how: on 19 November parliament ratified the military-technical pact with Kyiv, citing Ukraine's low-altitude detection expertise, while the General Staff admits it cannot shoot drones down. Over the next 90 days, expect more crossings whenever Russia strikes Odesa, Vinnytsia and western Ukraine, along with repeat airspace closures, protests to the Russian embassy and a crash or wreckage on Moldovan soil, which remains a realistic possibility. Expect faster counter-drone procurement with EU and Ukrainian help, and continued Russian hybrid pressure through Gagauzia, where the governor runoff is on 29 November, and Transnistria's winter energy squeeze. A first fatality, damage to critical infrastructure or evidence of deliberate targeting would justify a review toward HIGH.

forecasts.statement: A Russian drone or missile, or identifiable wreckage of one, falls on Moldovan territory (crash or impact, not only an overflight).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Moldova's Defence Ministry or police report a crash, impact or recovered wreckage of a Russian drone or missile on Moldovan territory, as reported by Reuters, AP or Moldovan official channels.

forecasts.statement: Moldovan authorities again close all or part of the national airspace to civil aviation because of a drone or missile threat (a closure separate from the 17 November 2026 one).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Moldova's Civil Aviation Authority, Defence Ministry or government announces a new airspace closure or restriction for civil aviation because of drones or missiles by that date, as reported by Reuters, AP, Euronews or Moldovan official channels.

countries.name: Georgia
incidents: 22–23 Nov — Tbilisi: President Kavelashvili pardoned 232 convicts on St George's Day, but only three were political prisoners: Giorgi Mindadze, Anri Kvaratskhelia and Nikoloz Javakhishvili. Activist Giorgi Okmelashvili, jailed over the 2024 foreign-agents protests, was also freed (Caucasian Knot).

23 Nov — Tbilisi: Pro-European protests outside parliament and the city assembly reached their 726th day, with at least 200 people demanding new elections, the release of political prisoners and the repeal of repressive laws. Organisers are building toward the 28 November anniversary rally (Caucasian Knot).

25 Nov — Batumi: At the Constitutional Court hearing on Georgian Dream's lawsuit to ban five opposition parties, Chairman Nadaraia again ordered Coalition for Change leader Nika Gvaramia out of the courtroom. The hearing was postponed to 30 November after a judge's father died (JAMnews).

25 Nov — Brussels/Tbilisi: The European Commission proposed removing Georgia's Kulevi oil refinery from the Russia sanctions list, which PM Kobakhidze welcomed. The same day, UNM member Anatoli Gigauri was released after serving two years on protest-related charges (JAMnews).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There is no organised political violence. The government combined small gestures, freeing three political prisoners among 232 pardons, with continued pressure in the Batumi party-ban hearing, where Gvaramia was again expelled before the hearing was adjourned to 30 November. Daily protests remain peaceful at a few hundred people. The 28 November second anniversary of the suspended EU accession bid is the most likely flashpoint for larger crowds and forceful dispersal in the coming days. Over the next 90 days, the party-ban ruling remains the key variable. The court has rejected nearly every defence motion, so a ruling banning at least one party before mid-February remains a realistic possibility, though the June 2027 deadline lets the court take its time. Expect selective pardons alongside new criminal cases against opposition figures and journalists, tactical EU engagement on energy (Kulevi) alongside deeper political estrangement, and routine detentions along the South Ossetia line. Banning the main opposition parties combined with mass protests that are violently dispersed would justify HIGH.

forecasts.statement: Georgia's Constitutional Court rules to ban (declare unconstitutional) at least one of the five opposition parties named in the Georgian Dream petition.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Civil.ge, Georgia Today, JAMnews or Reuters reports a Constitutional Court ruling banning at least one of UNM, Coalition for Change, Strong Georgia/Lelo, the Federalists or Gakharia for Georgia by that date.

countries.name: Armenia
incidents: 23 Nov — Yerevan: Pashinyan published the draft of Armenia's new constitution, said it would secure peace, and vowed to resign if voters reject it (Public Radio of Armenia). Opposition factions, including the Armenia Alliance, said they would not provide the votes needed to send the draft to a referendum, for which Civil Contract lacks a two-thirds majority (Armenpress).

23 Nov — Syunik/Washington: Pashinyan and Trump announced the launch of the practical phase of the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) linking mainland Azerbaijan with Nakhchivan through Syunik. Deputy Foreign Minister Kostanyan said on 25 November that rail construction would start in 2027, and Iranian adviser Mokhber warned against routes bypassing Iran (Armenian Weekly, JAMnews).

25–26 Nov — Yerevan/Moscow: Deputy PM Mher Grigoryan held talks with Russian Deputy PM Overchuk in Moscow, and the Kremlin said it is preparing for Pashinyan's 3 December working visit. Moscow wants him to say whether he will attend the 22 December CIS summit in St Petersburg (Public Radio of Armenia, JAMnews).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There were no new deaths or clashes. The confrontation has moved to the constitution itself: Pashinyan published the draft on 23 November and staked his job on it. The opposition, which holds the blocking third, says it will not let it go to a referendum and frames it as the 'Aliyev constitution', while Pashinyan has hinted at early elections to break the deadlock. TRIPP's 'practical phase' launch with Trump keeps the peace track moving, but signing the treaty still hinges on the referendum. Over the next 90 days, expect a parliamentary standoff over the referendum vote, rising pressure on opposition MPs, continued court cases against the Karapetyan family and other opposition figures, and Moscow amplifying opposition grievances around Pashinyan's 3 December visit and the CIS summit. Parliament approving a referendum before late February is unlikely, which makes a snap-election gambit more plausible. Protests should stay largely non-violent. Violent street unrest, a deliberate shooting or armed border incidents would warrant a review toward HIGH.

forecasts.statement: Armenia's National Assembly adopts a decision to put the draft new constitution to a national referendum (the two-thirds vote required under the current constitution).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Armenpress, Azatutyun (RFE/RL), OC Media or Reuters reports that parliament has voted to submit the draft constitution to a referendum by that date. A government announcement, a draft decision or a vote that fails does not count.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
incidents: 19 Nov — Baku: Human rights defender Bashir Suleymanli was sentenced to 7.5 years in prison, and Human Rights Watch called for his release (JAMnews).

24–25 Nov — Baku: In the closed trial of Popular Front leader Ali Karimli and deputy Mammad Ibrahim on charges of attempting to seize power by force, relatives of former presidential administration head Ramiz Mehdiyev testified on 24 November and the hearing was adjourned for further witnesses. Both defendants deny the charges (1news.az, JAMnews).

24–25 Nov — Iğdır (Türkiye): Aliyev and Erdoğan backed the 'Zangezur corridor' at the International Caucasus Congress. Foreign Minister Bayramov said Baku hopes TRIPP will be implemented soon, and Aliyev said over 100,000 tonnes of cargo had transited Azerbaijan to Armenia over the past year (Armenian Weekly, JAMnews).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. This was another quiet week with no hostilities. Domestic repression continued through the courts, with the Suleymanli sentence and the closed Karimli 'seizure of power' trial, which has moved into witness testimony tied to the Mehdiyev case. Abroad, Baku is busy: it backs the Zangezur/TRIPP route with Ankara, signed a strategic partnership with Lithuania and prepared an EU partnership agreement, while still requiring Armenia to change its constitution before signing the treaty. Over the next 90 days, expect the Karimli trial to stay closed, with a conviction likely whenever a verdict comes, and continued international criticism, including over Baku's OSCE chairmanship in 2027. Expect recurring smuggling incidents on the Iranian border and sharper rhetoric with Tehran over TRIPP. The peace track will move slowly and hinge on Armenia's stalled referendum. Violent clashes during protests, or a pattern of armed incidents on the Armenian or Iranian border, would warrant a review toward HIGH.

forecasts.statement: The Baku Court of Grave Crimes delivers a verdict convicting Popular Front leader Ali Karimli on the charge of attempting to seize power by force.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Turan, APA, 1news.az, JAMnews, OC Media or RFE/RL reports a guilty verdict and sentence for Ali Karimli in this case by that date. Adjournments or an acquittal do not count.

regions.name: Sahel
overview: Sudan's drone war hit Blue Nile hardest this week. On 24 November drone strikes that the rights group Emergency Lawyers attributed to the RSF killed at least 19 civilians in three residential neighbourhoods of Ed Damazin; a Sudan Tribune source gave at least 14. The same day drones targeted the Roseires dam and power facilities. In West Kordofan the army said on 20 November it had dismantled RSF positions in 10 areas around Al-Nahud and Abu Zabad during a week-long offensive, but no source shows it entering Al-Nahud. Army aircraft also struck RSF headquarters in Nyala on 19 November.

In Mali, JNIM attacked army and Africa Corps positions in Niono (Ségou region) on 21 November. Gunfire and explosions hit the town's referral health centre; MSF treated 26 wounded and one health worker was killed. RFI reported about thirty dead in total, and the competing army and JNIM tolls are disputed. The army then announced strikes on 20–24 November at Tinzaouatène, Talhandak, Farabougou and north-east of Niono, claiming more than 40 fighters killed. Crisis Group (20 Nov) noted JNIM's announced 'second phase' aimed at major towns and fuel convoys.

Niger's south-east flared: Boko Haram attacked a patrol near Baroua (Diffa) on 24 November, killing 11 soldiers according to the defence ministry. A Saudi national was reportedly abducted between Tillabéri and Niamey on 21–22 November, with suspicion falling on IS Sahel. Burkina Faso remained under a near-total information blackout; the only in-window item is a JNIM claim to have overrun a militia position at Selmagui (Kaya area) on 22 November. A Reuters review of ACLED data (25 Nov) counted 187 JNIM drone attacks since 2023.

In Nigeria, communal and reprisal violence in Borgu LGA (Niger State) became the region's deadliest event of the week outside Sudan. An attack on Lumma Ba'are on 21 November killed five, including the village head; reprisal raids on Fulani communities followed, which MACBAN said killed 64 and Reuters residents put at at least 30 on 24 November. Air strikes in Borno continued (eight ISWAP fighters claimed at Tumbuna, 23 Nov). Chad's Tibesti conflict continued without a ceasefire, and Mauritania recorded no armed incident.

countries.name: Mali
incidents: 21 Nov — Niono, Ségou region: JNIM attacked several army and Russian Africa Corps positions, including the town's main military installations. Gunfire and heavy-weapon explosions hit the referral health centre, killing one health worker; MSF treated 26 wounded. RFI reported about thirty dead in total, including one civilian; the army disputes JNIM's claimed toll.

Night of 20–21 Nov — Tinzaouatène, Kidal region: The army general staff said a strike on an ammunition depot 'neutralised' 23 fighters and destroyed the stock and a pick-up, and a second strike destroyed an illegal gold-processing site. Not independently verified.

Night of 22–23 Nov — Talhandak and Tinzaouatène, Kidal region: The army said strikes destroyed a depot with more than 90 motorcycles and spare parts at Talhandak and killed 11 fighters at Tinzaouatène; on 23 Nov it also struck armed men and two trucks near Farabougou (Ségou). Army figures only.

23–24 Nov — North-east of Niono and other areas: The army said strikes linked to the hunt for the Niono attackers killed about ten fighters and destroyed seven motorcycles, according to APA. Not independently verified.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The Niono assault shows JNIM can still hit fortified army and Africa Corps camps in the Office du Niger heartland, close to the Ségou–Bamako axis. Crisis Group reports that JNIM's announced 'second phase' targets major towns, fuel convoys and military bases. FAMa is answering with an intensive air campaign, from Tinzaouatène and Talhandak near the Algerian border to Ségou and Mopti, and will likely keep claiming large tolls that cannot be verified. Over the next 90 days JNIM is likely to keep up attacks on garrisons and supply routes in Ségou, Mopti and Kayes. A JNIM attack on a fuel convoy killing ten or more people remains a realistic possibility while Bamako depends on escorted tanker convoys. An attack inside Bamako district itself is unlikely, but cannot be ruled out given JNIM's stated focus on major towns. IS Sahel violence around Ménaka is likely to continue. Watch for further attacks on health facilities, a renewed tightening of the blockade, and signs of strain in the junta.

events.place: North-east of Niono and other areas

forecasts.statement: JNIM attacks a fuel tanker convoy anywhere in Mali in an incident that reportedly kills ten or more people (drivers, escorts or civilians).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, RFI or ACLED reports a single JNIM attack on a fuel convoy in Mali on or before 31 Jan 2027 with a reported toll of at least ten dead.

forecasts.statement: JNIM carries out an armed attack, IED or drone attack inside Bamako district (the capital city itself, not its surrounding region).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, RFI or ACLED reports, on or before 26 Feb 2027, an attack inside Bamako district occurring after 26 Nov 2026 that is claimed by or credibly attributed to JNIM (blockade checkpoints outside the district do not count).

countries.name: Niger
incidents: 24 Nov — Near Baroua, Diffa region: Boko Haram fighters attacked an army patrol, killing 11 soldiers and wounding five, according to a provisional defence ministry toll reported by AFP. The ministry said 22 attackers were 'neutralised'.

21–22 Nov — Between Tillabéri and Niamey: A Saudi national was reportedly kidnapped by fighters suspected of belonging to IS Sahel, two security sources told Reuters. No group has claimed it and the authorities have not commented.

24–25 Nov — Niamey: Gen. Tiani opened the first 'Invest in Niger' forum and received the trade ministers of Burkina Faso and Mali, underlining AES economic integration amid the junta's isolation since the August mutiny.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Niger faces large-scale violence on two fronts: IS Sahel and JNIM in Tillabéri and the Tahoua–Dosso belt (at least 37 civilians killed at Tillim on 12 November), and Boko Haram/ISWAP in Diffa, where 11 soldiers died near Baroua on 24 November. Over the next 90 days, another single attack in Tillabéri killing 20 or more people is likely. Further deadly attacks on army patrols and posts around Diffa and the Komadugu Yobe are likely as dry-season mobility improves; another single Diffa attack killing ten or more soldiers is a realistic possibility. The kidnapping of a Saudi national near Niamey shows that abduction of foreigners remains a live threat close to the capital. The junta is leaning on AES integration and Algerian fuel and military links. After the August mutiny and the purges that followed, another coup attempt or mutiny remains a realistic risk.

forecasts.statement: A single armed attack in Niger's Tillabéri region kills 20 or more people (civilians, soldiers or both).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, RFI, ACLED or an official Nigerien statement reports, on or before 31 Jan 2027, a single attack in Tillabéri region occurring after 19 Nov 2026 with a reported toll of at least 20 dead (attackers' own losses excluded).

forecasts.statement: A single attack by Boko Haram or ISWAP in Niger's Diffa region kills ten or more Nigerien soldiers or security personnel.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, RFI, ACLED or an official Nigerien statement reports, on or before 26 Feb 2027, a single attack in Diffa region occurring after 26 Nov 2026 in which at least ten soldiers, gendarmes or guards were killed.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
incidents: 22 Nov — Selmagui, Kaya area (Centre-North): JNIM claimed it took control of a position of state-backed VDP militia in the evening, according to claims relayed by the Sahel Alerte monitoring account. No toll was given and the claim cannot be independently verified.

25 Nov — Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger: A Reuters review of ACLED data found JNIM had carried out 187 drone attacks between 2023 and mid-November 2026 (235 including the FLA). JNIM has used them against army positions such as Djibo in Burkina Faso.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. JNIM keeps claiming small attacks on army and VDP positions across the Centre-North, North and Boucle du Mouhoun (Djondougou, Sebasi and Selmagui in November), and its growing use of commercial drones adds a new threat to garrisons. The JNIM–IS Sahel war in Oudalan continues. The fall in mass-casualty attacks since late June reflects operational choices rather than reduced capability. Over the next 90 days the dry season is likely to bring renewed large garrison assaults; a single attack killing 20 or more soldiers, VDP or civilians is likely. Sieges of towns such as Djibo are likely to persist. Repression of dissent and abuses against Fulani communities will likely continue. Given the blackout, analysts should rely on group claims, rights-group reporting and ACLED data, and treat all tolls with caution.

forecasts.statement: A single JNIM attack on a military, VDP or civilian target in Burkina Faso is reported to have killed 20 or more people (attackers excluded).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, RFI, HRW or ACLED reports, on or before 31 Jan 2027, a single attack in Burkina Faso occurring after 26 Nov 2026 attributed to JNIM with a reported toll of at least 20 dead among soldiers, VDP and/or civilians (a JNIM claim alone does not count).

countries.name: Sudan
incidents: 24 Nov — Ed Damazin, Blue Nile: Drone strikes on three residential neighbourhoods killed at least 19 civilians from three families and wounded 15, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers, which blamed the RSF (Reuters). Sudan Tribune, citing a local civil-society group, gave at least 14 dead. The RSF did not comment.

24 Nov — Roseires, Blue Nile: Earlier the same day, drones targeted the Roseires dam and power facilities, wounding five civilians. Emergency Lawyers warned of possible disruption to Blue Nile's electricity and the national grid.

20 Nov — Around Al-Nahud and Abu Zabad, West Kordofan: The army said it had dismantled RSF defences in 10 areas during a week-long offensive, after seizing five localities around Al-Sa'atat on 16 Nov; the Joint Force said it retook eight areas. The RSF still holds Al-Nahud.

19 Nov — Nyala, South Darfur: Army aircraft struck what Sudan Tribune described as RSF headquarters after drones circled the city for more than 45 minutes. Residents heard three loud explosions in northern and eastern Nyala, and fighters including an officer were reportedly killed or wounded.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: full-scale war continues on several fronts. In West Kordofan the army and the Joint Force are working through RSF defences around Al-Nahud and Abu Zabad, but have not yet entered Al-Nahud, which the RSF still holds along with most of the state. Taking Al-Nahud in the next 90 days remains a realistic possibility rather than a likely outcome. Blue Nile is now the main theatre of the RSF's drone campaign. After Bani Shako, the 24 November strikes on Ed Damazin and on the Roseires dam and power plant show the RSF can hit the state capital and critical infrastructure. Further RSF strikes on Blue Nile towns and power infrastructure are highly likely, and an army recapture of Sali in this period remains unlikely. The army will likely keep striking RSF command sites in Nyala and across Darfur, with a standing risk of civilian casualties. RSF attacks on Joint Force positions around Kornoi in North Darfur are likely to continue. With continuing foreign arms flows and no credible talks, a truce is unlikely. Expect more displacement toward Darfur, Chad, South Sudan and Ethiopia, and deepening famine conditions.

events.place: Around Al-Nahud and Abu Zabad, West Kordofan

forecasts.statement: The Sudanese Armed Forces and allied forces retake the Sali military base in Blue Nile from the RSF–SPLM-N alliance.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Sudan Tribune, Dabanga, Sudans Post, Reuters or AP reports, on or before 12 Feb 2027, that SAF or allied forces have regained control of Sali (an SAF claim corroborated by footage or a second independent source counts).

forecasts.statement: The Sudanese Armed Forces and allied forces (including the Joint Force) take control of the town of Al-Nahud in West Kordofan from the RSF.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Sudan Tribune, Sudans Post, Dabanga, Reuters or AP reports, on or before 19 Feb 2027, that SAF or allied forces control Al-Nahud town (an SAF claim corroborated by footage or a second independent source counts).

countries.name: Chad
incidents: 19 Nov — Tibesti: RFI reported that fighting between the army and the Miski Self-Defence Committee continues. Signatories of the April 2025 Miski accord, including the MADAT rebel movement, accuse the government of not honouring it and cite air strikes and a blockade. N'Djamena calls its campaign a law-and-order operation and says dialogue channels remain open.

21 Nov — Abéché, Ouaddaï: The Coordination of the Eastern Operational Zones displayed 450 weapons, about 15,250 rounds of ammunition and 201 magazines seized in Adré, Birak, Haraz, Tissi and on Abéché patrols, reflecting the flow of arms along the Sudan border.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The Miski conflict has become a war of attrition. Government drone and air strikes and a blockade face a militia that still controls the town, and the reported loss of 23 soldiers at Arkinya on 10 November (unconfirmed) suggests the army is paying a high price. The other signatories of the 2025 accord now openly say the government has broken it, which raises the risk of wider northern armed opposition. Over the next 90 days, continued strikes on Miski are likely, but a full army takeover of the town remains unlikely. The arms seized in Ouaddaï underline the flow of weapons from the Sudan war into the east. Dry-season transhumance is likely to bring further deadly intercommunal clashes in the centre and east, and Boko Haram activity around Lake Chad continues. Confirmed heavy losses in Tibesti, other armed groups joining the Miski fight, or repeated large cross-border strikes from Sudan would justify CRITICAL.

forecasts.statement: The Chadian army takes control of the town of Miski in Tibesti from the Miski Self-Defence Committee, by force or under a negotiated handover.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if AFP, Reuters, RFI or Crisis Group reports on or before 12 Feb 2027 that Chadian state forces control Miski town.

countries.name: Mauritania
incidents: 23 Nov — Off Nouadhibou: The navy rescued a boat carrying 93 migrants (69 men, 17 women, seven minors) bound for the Canary Islands, the army said. A week earlier coast guards intercepted a canoe from Bargny, Senegal, carrying 179 people.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Mauritania has suffered no jihadist attack since 2011. Its exposure comes from the deterioration in Mali, including JNIM's escalation in Ségou and Kayes, the large Malian refugee population in Hodh Chargui, and incidents involving Mauritanian herders and FAMa or Africa Corps units along the border. The Atlantic migration route to the Canaries keeps the navy busy and keeps cooperation with Spain and the EU high on the agenda. Over the next 90 days, Malian army and JNIM activity in western Mali is likely to push more refugees into Hodh Chargui and keep relations with Bamako tense, while Nouakchott continues containment through diplomacy and border deployments. A JNIM attack inside Mauritania or an armed border clash would justify HIGH; neither is likely in this period.

countries.name: Nigeria
incidents: 21 Nov — Lumma Ba'are, Borgu LGA, Niger State: Attackers killed five people, including the village head, injured five and burned houses, according to the state information commissioner (AP). Residents assumed the attackers were Fulani; local media reported one arrest.

22–24 Nov — Fulani communities in Borgu LGA, Niger State: Reprisal raids, reportedly by more than 300 people from Lumma Ba'are, followed. MACBAN said 64 people from Fulani communities were killed over the weekend, and residents told Reuters at least 30 were killed and homes burned on 24 Nov. Amnesty International said it had videos of children being killed. There is no official toll.

22 Nov — Qua'an Pan LGA, Plateau: Gunmen attacked a herding community, reportedly killing at least four herders and rustling more than 100 cattle (Parrot Nigeria). A curfew was imposed in Qua'an Pan the next evening after further violence, and houses were razed in Bong, Doemak district.
23 Nov — Tumbuna, Abadam LGA, Borno: Two air strikes at about 1 a.m. reportedly killed eight ISWAP fighters, according to military-sourced reports. Not independently verified.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The Borgu killings show how quickly farmer–herder grievances in Niger State can escalate into tit-for-tat massacres. Borgu also borders Kainji Lake National Park, where jihadist and bandit groups operate, so further reprisals are likely; a new attack there killing ten or more people within the next two months is likely. Plateau continues to see repeated deadly raids and reprisals in Mangu, Bokkos and now Qua'an Pan, and Zamfara bandits keep killing and abducting civilians. In the north-east, ISWAP is likely to keep up night raids and drone attacks on forward bases in Kukawa, Marte, Monguno and the Lake Chad islands. A single attack on a military base killing ten or more soldiers is likely, while the military keeps claiming high enemy tolls from air strikes. As the election cycle advances, attacks on campaign events and officials are a growing risk.

events.place: Lumma Ba'are, Borgu LGA, Niger State
Fulani communities in Borgu LGA, Niger State

forecasts.statement: ISWAP or Boko Haram fighters attack a military base or forward position in Borno or Yobe in a single attack that reportedly kills ten or more Nigerian soldiers.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, HumAngle, Premium Times or Daily Trust reports, on or before 12 Feb 2027, a single attack in Borno or Yobe in which at least ten soldiers were killed (military, security-source or credible local tolls count).

forecasts.statement: A single attack in Borgu LGA, Niger State, kills ten or more people (civilians, herders or security forces).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, Premium Times, Daily Trust or HumAngle reports, on or before 31 Jan 2027, a single attack in Borgu LGA occurring after 26 Nov 2026 with a reported toll of at least ten dead (official, residents' or community-group tolls count).

regions.name: Asia-Pacific
overview: The summit season ended without a strategic reset. At their 19 November bilateral in Shenzhen, Xi told Trump the US must do 'the right thing' on Taiwan, and Xinhua said Trump stated the US 'does not support Taiwan independence'. The White House had not confirmed that line. The first Xi–Trump–Putin trilateral produced a statement on UN reform, energy and non-proliferation, but nothing on Taiwan or Ukraine. Military pressure resumed straight after the summit. Taiwan's MND tracked 24 PLA aircraft and 12 ships in the report of 22 November and 10 Chinese balloons over three days before the 28 November local elections. The AFP counted 48 Chinese coast guard and navy vessels in the West Philippine Sea in the week after the ASEAN summit and confirmed an H-6 bomber flight.

Russia's long-range aviation became a regional factor in its own right. On 17 November Japan said two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace near Okinoshima. Two Tu-95MS bombers flew home from Da Nang on 19 November and were intercepted by Japan and Taiwan. On 24 November Russian bombers, reported as Tu-160s, entered the KADIZ about 24 km from Ulleungdo, which triggered South Korea's first-ever preemptive air-raid alert on the island. Meanwhile Kim Jong Un toured nuclear-material and weapons facilities (KCNA, 26 November) and called for tactical nuclear weapons 'across multiple domains', after ignoring Trump's overtures. He also expelled the Swiss envoy over sanctions on a children's camp. No ballistic launch was reported.

South Asia stayed the most violent part of the region. In Bangladesh, Hasina said on 24 November that she will return on 16 December, and the government vowed to arrest her. Arson and crude-bomb attacks spread to more than 20 districts, with tit-for-tat burning of more than 50 Awami League homes in Narail and another shooting death and a factional killing on 25–26 November. Garment-wage clashes in Gazipur added a second flashpoint. In Pakistan, ISPR reported dozens more militants killed, including 15 in Mastung on 21 November and 12 more in Balochistan around 25–26 November, while the BLA claimed 20 personnel killed in drone and other attacks. Pakistan–Taliban relations worsened further over alleged cross-border drone activity.

In Myanmar, the ICJ ruled on 19 November that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the first such finding against a state. The junta rejected the ruling, and the UK added sanctions and an aviation-fuel ban. Regime airstrikes continued in Rakhine, including the killing of four civilians and an infant in Pauktaw on 21–22 November, and fighting intensified around Kyaukphyu. In Indonesia, Jakarta relabelled the TPNPB an 'Armed Extremist Group'. A teacher was shot dead in Beoga, three TPNPB fighters were killed in Nduga, and rice boats bound for Yahukimo came under fire, all ahead of the 1 December anniversary. India's J&K and Manipur produced only small-scale incidents, and Thailand's south saw a coordinated attack on CCTV cameras.

countries.name: North Korea
incidents: 26 Nov — Undisclosed sites: KCNA said Kim Jong Un inspected nuclear-material production and weapons research facilities. He called for tactical nuclear weapons to be deployed 'across multiple domains for different missions', said the country's nuclear status 'will never change' and warned that denying it would be 'an open declaration of war'. Bloomberg noted a rare display of warheads (Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera).

19 Nov — Yongbyon: The IAEA said North Korea is expanding a uranium enrichment facility (Al Jazeera). On 25 Nov NK News reported imagery suggesting the North tested an ICBM engine while Trump was seeking a meeting.

24–25 Nov — Pyongyang: North Korea condemned Swiss sanctions on the Songdowon children's camp, which is allegedly linked to transfers of children from occupied Ukraine. It declared Swiss office head Sylvain Astier persona non grata with 48 hours to leave and forced the office, reopened in late October, to close (Al Jazeera, Reuters).

22–23 Nov — Pyongyang: For the first time, Kim personally accepted credentials from new ambassadors, including those of India and the Philippines, and vowed to expand ties with 'friendly' states (NK News, WSJ, Inquirer). No ballistic missile launch was reported in the window.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Pyongyang answered the summit season with nuclear signalling rather than talks. Kim's facility tour and 'multiple domains' language, the IAEA's report of enrichment expansion and an apparent ICBM engine test point to a coming phase of delivery-system tests. Expelling the Swiss envoy and staging a credentials ceremony for 'friendly' states show a deliberate narrowing of contacts with the West. Over the next 90 days, a JCS-reported ballistic missile launch remains likely, possibly timed to the year-end party plenum, the new year or allied drills. Expect naval and cruise-missile trials linked to the 'multiple domains' tactical nuclear concept. A full ICBM flight test in the window is unlikely, but the engine test makes it a live option, and a nuclear test remains a low-probability wildcard. A Trump–Kim meeting is unlikely while Pyongyang demands recognition as a nuclear state. Ties with Moscow will deepen, including fuel payments, and cyber theft will keep funding the programme.

forecasts.statement: North Korea launches at least one ballistic missile that South Korea's JCS publicly reports.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the JCS (as reported by Yonhap, Reuters or AP) announces at least one North Korean ballistic missile launch between 2026-11-12 and 2026-12-31. Cruise-missile or artillery-only launches do not count.

forecasts.statement: North Korea conducts a flight test of an intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM), as identified by South Korea's JCS or Japan's Ministry of Defense.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, between 2026-11-26 and 2027-02-26, the JCS or Japan's MoD, as reported by Yonhap, Kyodo, Reuters or AP, assesses a North Korean launch as an ICBM, or KCNA announces an ICBM launch that one of them confirms. Engine ground tests, satellite launches and IRBM or hypersonic launches not classed as an ICBM do not count.

countries.name: Myanmar
incidents: 19 Nov — The Hague: The ICJ ruled in The Gambia v. Myanmar that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in 2017, the first time the court has found a state responsible for genocide. The junta rejected the ruling as unfair. On 24 Nov the UK sanctioned five military officers and announced a ban on aviation-fuel supplies (UN News, AP, Myanmar Now).

21–22 Nov — Pauktaw Township, Rakhine: Junta jets bombed Thawin Chaung and Nan Tet Kyun villages over the weekend, killing four civilians, including a five-month-old infant, and injuring 13, according to locals (Myanmar Now; Narinjara reported the strike under the AA name Wirathani).
