22–24 Nov — Ponnagyun Township, Rakhine: The AA said junta airstrikes on two villages killed two civilians, including a cattle herder, and injured one (Narinjara).

22 Nov — Kyaukphyu and Ngapyi Island, Rakhine: Narinjara reported intensified fighting around Kyaukphyu and said about 20 regime soldiers had been killed on Ngapyi Island in recent days. This is unverified and comes from an AA-aligned outlet.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The ICJ genocide ruling adds a lasting legal and sanctions cost, with UK measures including an aviation-fuel ban and a closed-door UNSC discussion, but it does not change behaviour on the ground. Air raids on Rakhine villages killed at least six civilians this week. Over the next 90 days, expect continued jet, gyrocopter and drone strikes on Rakhine, Sagaing, Magway and the southeast. Aviation-fuel restrictions may slowly constrain sortie rates but will not stop them. The AA's push on Kyaukphyu and its approaches, including Ngapyi and Ramree, will intensify. Kyaukphyu is a Chinese strategic interest, so expect Beijing to press both sides. A full AA capture of Sittwe in the window remains unlikely given the reinforced garrison and naval resupply. Northern Shan stays frozen under MNDAA consolidation, spillover into Thailand around Myawaddy will recur, and no negotiated de-escalation is in sight.

forecasts.statement: The Arakan Army takes full control of Sittwe, the Rakhine State capital, with junta forces withdrawn or defeated.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, The Irrawaddy or DVB report by 2027-02-12 that the AA controls Sittwe town and the regime's regional command there has fallen or withdrawn. AA claims alone do not count.

countries.name: Pakistan
incidents: 21 Nov — Mastung, Balochistan: Security forces said they killed 15 militants they called 'Fitna al-Hindustan' (Baloch separatists) in two operations under Radd-ul-Fitna-III, praised by PM Shehbaz Sharif and the Balochistan chief minister. On 26 Nov ISPR reported 12 more killed in Balochistan operations (Express Tribune, Aaj, Geo).

22–24 Nov — Balochistan: The BLA claimed it killed 20 Pakistani personnel in a series of attacks across the province, including armed-drone strikes, and Indian outlets reported a BLA attack that killed five FC personnel. Pakistan has not confirmed these claims and they are unverified (Hans India, News18).

21–24 Nov — Peshawar, Kohat and Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: A joint CTD–army raid killed three TTP militants on Peshawar's outskirts, and police killed three in Kohat. On 24 Nov the CTD killed five TTP militants in a Peshawar raid while a TTP commander escaped, and Operation Sarbulandi killed three more in Bannu (Arab News PK, Dunya, Bol News).

22 Nov — Pakistan–Afghanistan border: Islamabad warned the Taliban over alleged cross-border drone activity, and Kabul accused Pakistan of backing anti-Taliban armed groups. Pakistan excluded Afghanistan from a regional conference, and no ceasefire or border reopening was reported (Kabul Tribune, Arab News PK, Afghanistan International).
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The week was dominated by state-announced operations: 15 killed in Mastung, a string of CTD raids in Peshawar, Kohat and Bannu, and a further ISPR toll in Balochistan. The BLA answered with claims of 20 personnel killed, often by drone, that run well above official figures. The Taliban relationship is sliding from border fighting into proxy accusations, with Islamabad citing cross-border drone activity and Kabul alleging Pakistani support for anti-Taliban groups. Over the next 90 days, expect frequent TTP attacks on police and FC posts in Bannu, Lakki Marwat, Kohat, Dera Ismail Khan and the former tribal districts. The BLA is likely to keep up drone, IED and suicide attacks in Mastung, Kech, Nushki and Kharan and to disrupt highway and rail traffic, with a mass-casualty attack a realistic possibility. A Pakistani air or drone strike inside Afghanistan remains likely, especially after a major TTP attack.

events.place: Peshawar, Kohat and Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

forecasts.statement: Pakistan carries out at least one airstrike or drone strike inside Afghan territory.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or Al Jazeera report by 2027-02-12 a Pakistani air or drone strike on Afghan territory, confirmed by Pakistan or reported by the Taliban government. Cross-border artillery or small-arms fire alone does not count.

countries.name: India
incidents: 20 Nov — Imphal West, Manipur: Security forces killed a suspected KCP militant, reported to be an ex-serviceman, in a gunfight and arrested eight others, including a surrendered KCP-PWG chairman (The Hindu, NDTV, India Today NE).

22 Nov — Manipur: The families of the four victims of the October Nongshum ambush accepted the bodies after a month-long protest, once the government agreed to an 11-point charter of demands (Assam Tribune, Rediff). No new mass-casualty attack was found after the 13 Nov Ukhrul killings.

21–23 Nov — Jammu and Kashmir: Home Minister Amit Shah said 'not a single local terrorist' remains in the Kashmir Valley after the killing of LeT commander Lateef Bhat. Security officials say about 65 Pakistani militants are on their radar and claim the ISI is planning fresh attacks (Open, Mid-Day, Republic).
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The week was quieter than the last. Manipur saw a valley-based KCP encounter and a negotiated end to the Nongshum body standoff, but the Kuki–Naga confrontation that produced the 13 November Ukhrul ambush is unresolved and the Tangkhul ultimatum stands. Over the next 90 days, expect retaliatory shootings and ambushes along NH-2 and NH-202 (Senapati, Kangpokpi, Ukhrul, Noney), road blockades, operations against valley-based groups (KCP, PLA, UNLF factions) and continued displacement. A single attack killing five or more remains a realistic possibility. In J&K, the end of the local LeT cadre shifts the threat to roughly 65 Pakistani militants, mainly in the Kishtwar–Doda forests, where two SPOs were killed on 11–12 November. Expect sporadic ambushes on security forces even as winter reduces infiltration. India–Pakistan and India–China friction stays below the threshold of border clashes.

forecasts.statement: A single armed attack, ambush or clash in Manipur kills at least five people.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, PTI or a major Indian national outlet (The Hindu, Indian Express, NDTV) reports, between 2026-11-20 and 2027-01-31, one incident in Manipur (one attack, ambush or gunfight at one location on one day) with at least five people killed, including militants. Separate incidents may not be combined.

countries.name: China
incidents: 19 Nov — Shenzhen: At their bilateral talks Xi told Trump the US must do 'the right thing' on Taiwan to avoid 'great turbulence'. Xinhua said Trump stated the US 'does not support Taiwan independence', which the White House had not confirmed. The Xi–Trump–Putin trilateral issued a statement on UN reform, energy security and non-proliferation, without addressing Taiwan or Ukraine (RFA, SCMP, GMA/AP).

19 Nov — Antelope Reef, Paracel Islands: Analysts cited by AFP said a runway of nearly 3 km is being built on China's newly reclaimed island at Antelope Reef. It would be Beijing's second runway in the Paracels and part of the first major island-building since 2017 (Jiji, Kuwait Times).

21–22 Nov — Around Taiwan: After the summit, PLA activity reported by Taiwan's MND rose from two aircraft in the 21 Nov report to 24 aircraft, 12 ships and two balloons in the 22 Nov report, with 10 balloons detected over three days before Taiwan's 28 Nov local elections (Taiwan News, Taipei Times).

25 Nov — South China Sea: The Philippine military confirmed that a PLA H-6 bomber flew over the West Philippine Sea near the Philippine coast, as the AFP counted 48 Chinese coast guard and navy vessels in Philippine-claimed waters in the week after the ASEAN summit (Philstar, Manila Times, ABS-CBN).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Beijing pocketed favourable Taiwan language from Shenzhen, at least in its own readout, and immediately resumed pressure. Taiwan-area sorties and balloons picked up before the 28 November election, vessel numbers in the West Philippine Sea rose to 48, an H-6 bomber flew near Philippine waters, and Antelope Reef construction advanced. Over the next 90 days, expect Beijing to use the 'does not support independence' line to press Washington on arms sales and on Lai, while keeping coercive tools ready. A named encirclement exercise around Taiwan remains a realistic possibility, most likely in response to a US arms package or a Lai speech. CCG patrols at Kinmen, Scarborough and the Senkakus and Russia–China joint bomber flights will continue. The main risk remains an unplanned collision or intercept with Philippine, Japanese or US forces. China's own territory faces no armed threat.

countries.name: Taiwan
incidents: 19 Nov — Shenzhen: Xi warned Trump that the US must do 'the right thing' on Taiwan to avoid 'great turbulence', and Xinhua reported Trump saying the US does not support Taiwan independence, which the White House had not confirmed (RFA, GMA/AP).

19 Nov — Taiwan ADIZ: The MND reported two Russian Tu-95 bombers entering Taiwan's ADIZ on their return from Vietnam, the second Russian approach that week, and Taiwan and Japan scrambled jets (Reuters via WMBD, The Aviationist).

21–22 Nov — Around Taiwan: The MND tracked 24 PLA aircraft, 12 ships and two balloons in the 24 hours to 22 Nov, up from two aircraft the day before, and detected 10 Chinese balloons over three days in the run-up to the 28 Nov local elections (Taiwan News, Taipei Times).
26 Nov — Around Taiwan: Two days before the local elections, the MND tracked six PLA naval ships and two military aircraft (Taiwan News).
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The post-summit pattern is pressure without spectacle. A 24-aircraft day, balloon waves and steady naval presence came before the 28 November elections, while Beijing's account of the Trump–Xi talks puts Taipei on the defensive diplomatically. Russian Tu-95s in the ADIZ add a new, if marginal, actor. Over the next 90 days, expect election-related cognitive operations and, if the DPP does well, a punitive response. A named PLA exercise remains a realistic possibility, as does a single-day spike of 45 or more sorties, most likely after a US arms announcement or a Lai New Year address. Expect continued CCG pressure on Kinmen and Pratas, balloon overflights through winter, and a close reading in Taipei of any US clarification of the 'does not support independence' line.

forecasts.statement: The PLA Eastern Theater Command announces a named large-scale military exercise around Taiwan (in the style of Strait Thunder or Justice Mission).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by 2027-02-12, the PLA Eastern Theater Command or Chinese state media publicly announce a drill around Taiwan under a specific exercise name, as reported by Reuters, AP or Taiwan's MND. Unannounced surges and routine 'joint combat readiness patrols' do not count.

forecasts.statement: Taiwan's MND reports at least 45 PLA aircraft sorties around Taiwan in a single daily (24-hour) report.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if any MND daily 'PLA activities in the waters and airspace around Taiwan' release issued between 2026-11-20 and 2027-01-31 reports 45 or more PLA aircraft sorties, as published by the MND or reported by Focus Taiwan, Taipei Times, Reuters or AP.

countries.name: Philippines
incidents: 24 Nov — Off Panata Island, Spratlys: The PCG said a Chinese maritime militia vessel made dangerous manoeuvres against BRP Cabra and its RHIB and nearly collided with them, while the PCG ordered out two militia vessels anchored in Philippine territorial waters (PNA, Manila Bulletin, ABS-CBN).
17–23 Nov — West Philippine Sea: The AFP said Chinese coast guard and navy vessels in the West Philippine Sea rose to 48 in the week after the ASEAN summit (ABS-CBN, Inquirer).
25 Nov — West Philippine Sea: The AFP confirmed that a Chinese H-6 bomber flew over the West Philippine Sea near the Philippine coast (Philstar, Manila Times).
23 Nov — Kidapawan City, Cotabato: The police chief of Bubong, Lanao del Sur, was shot dead inside a boarding house. The PNP ordered a manhunt and named four suspects (Inquirer, Philstar).
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The summit lull ended within days. Chinese hulls in the WPS rose to 48, a militia vessel nearly collided with BRP Cabra off Panata, and an H-6 bomber flight showed the air dimension. Beijing-linked academic claims to Batanes keep a northern flank in play. Washington's new defence investment does not offset Trump's non-committal Manila remarks. Over the next 90 days, renewed CCG blocking and water-cannon use against BFAR, PCG and resupply missions at Scarborough, Second Thomas and Sabina Shoals is likely. Expect more militia swarming near Pag-asa and Panata, PLA air patrols over the WPS, and expanding Philippine–Japanese–US cooperation at sea. In Mindanao and the BARMM, targeted killings of officials, clan feuds and small NPA and Dawlah Islamiyah clashes keep violence at a steady low level. A fatal incident at sea would trigger Mutual Defense Treaty consultations.

forecasts.statement: China Coast Guard vessels fire water cannon at a Philippine government vessel (PCG, BFAR or Navy) in the South China Sea.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, by 2027-02-12, the PCG, the AFP or the Philippine NSC report a CCG water-cannon use against a Philippine government vessel, as carried by Reuters, AP or Philippine national media.

countries.name: South Korea
incidents: 24 Nov — Ulleungdo, East Sea: Russian warplanes, reported as Tu-160 bombers, entered the KADIZ and came within about 24 km of Ulleungdo, prompting fighter scrambles and a first-ever preemptive air-raid alert on the island. The JCS said there was no airspace violation, and the foreign ministry expressed regret to Moscow (Yonhap, Korea JoongAng Daily, Chosun Ilbo).

23 Nov — Seoul: President Lee nominated new foreign and unification ministers and a new intelligence chief, a shake-up linked to strained intelligence ties with Washington and the deadlock with Pyongyang (NK News, Bloomberg, Straits Times).

19–26 Nov — Inter-Korean border: No North Korean missile launch, MDL crossing or warning-shot incident was found. Kim's 26 Nov call to widen tactical nuclear deployment and his warning that denying the North's nuclear status means 'war' were the main signals from Pyongyang.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The threat picture is widening beyond the DMZ. Russian bomber flights close to Ulleungdo forced Seoul's first preemptive civil alert, Kim's nuclear rhetoric hardened, and Lee's security-team overhaul signals an effort to repair intelligence ties with Washington before the wartime operational control transfer. Over the next 90 days, North Korean SRBM or cruise-missile launches toward the East Sea remain likely, and new South Korean warning shots at North Korean troops crossing the MDL remain likely, although winter may slow fortification work. Expect further Russian, and possibly joint Russia–China, KADIZ entries. Watch for live fire across the MDL, mine or drone incidents, launches toward the NLL, and any North Korean move to test the new ministers.

forecasts.statement: South Korean troops fire warning shots at North Korean soldiers crossing the Military Demarcation Line.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the JCS, as reported by Yonhap, Korea JoongAng Daily, Reuters or AP, confirms at least one new warning-shot incident against North Korean troops crossing the MDL between 2026-11-12 and 2027-01-31.

countries.name: Vietnam
incidents: 19 Nov — Da Nang: Two Russian Tu-95MS bombers, which had landed at Da Nang on 17 Nov with Il-78 tankers, left Vietnam and were intercepted by Japan and Taiwan on the way home. Analysts flagged the use of a civilian airport for strategic aviation (Washington Post, The Aviationist, EurAsian Times).

19 Nov — Antelope Reef, Paracel Islands: Analysts cited by AFP said China is building a runway of nearly 3 km on its new artificial island at Antelope Reef in the Vietnam-claimed Paracels (Jiji, Kuwait Times). On 25 Nov RFA reported that China is pushing its claims through 'patriotic cruises' to the Paracels.
22 Nov — Gulf of Tonkin: The Chinese and Vietnamese navies completed a joint patrol, with PLA anti-submarine ships taking part (SCMP).
24 Nov — Japan–Vietnam: The two governments discussed joint production of defence equipment (Indo-Pacific Defense Forum).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Hanoi's hedging was visible this week. It hosted Russian strategic bombers at Da Nang, completed a joint patrol with the PLA in the Gulf of Tonkin and discussed defence co-production with Japan, while China advanced a runway at Antelope Reef in the Vietnam-claimed Paracels. Over the next 90 days, expect Vietnamese diplomatic protests over Paracel construction and 'patriotic cruises', continued Vietnamese Spratly reclamation, and showcase defence diplomacy at the December defence expo. Possible US and Japanese concern over further Russian use of Vietnamese airfields is another watch point. CCG harassment or detention of Vietnamese fishermen in the Paracels is likely to recur, but a direct naval confrontation remains unlikely.

countries.name: Japan
incidents: 19 Nov — Shenzhen: PM Takaichi met Putin at APEC two days after Japan said two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace near Okinoshima for about three minutes. She also said she wants 'constructive and stable' ties with China, but Japanese commentators described her as snubbed by Beijing at the summit (The Diplomat, CNA, JAPAN Forward).
19 Nov — Sea of Japan / East China Sea: ASDF fighters scrambled to intercept two Russian Tu-95 bombers flying back from Vietnam (Defence Blog, The Aviationist).
23 Nov — Tokyo: The government moved to strengthen the coast guard with more patrol boats and drones to counter China (Nikkei Asia).
26 Nov — Senkaku Islands: Japan warned Chinese ships to leave the waters near the disputed islands (AFP via ABS-CBN).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained; watch for an upgrade. Japan now faces coercive air and sea activity from two directions. Russia violated Japanese airspace on 17 November and flew bomber transits on 19 and 24 November, while China kept its Senkaku pressure 'normalised' and the diplomatic freeze outlasted APEC. Tokyo is responding with coast guard expansion and a planned Type 25 hypersonic deployment on Hokkaido. Over the next 90 days, further CCG entries into Senkaku territorial waters are likely. Expect more PLAN and drone transits of the Ryukyu gaps, possible Russia–China joint bomber patrols, and North Korean launches into the Sea of Japan. A new airspace violation by Russian or Chinese aircraft is a realistic possibility. A radar lock-on, a close-quarters intercept or a missile impact in Japan's EEZ would justify raising Japan to HIGH.

events.place: Sea of Japan / East China Sea

forecasts.statement: Japan's Ministry of Defense reports a new violation of Japanese territorial airspace by a Russian or Chinese military aircraft or drone.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, between 2026-11-27 and 2027-02-26, Japan's MoD or Joint Staff announces that a Russian or Chinese military aircraft or drone (including a suspected one) entered Japanese territorial airspace, as reported by Kyodo, NHK, Reuters or AP. ADIZ entries, close approaches and balloon sightings without an airspace violation do not count.

countries.name: Indonesia
incidents: 20 Nov — Nduga, Highland Papua: The TNI said three TPNPB members, described as leading figures, were killed in a firefight with Rajawali and combat reconnaissance troops (ANTARA, Okezone).

22–23 Nov — Beoga and Ilaga, Puncak: Gunmen attributed to the TPNPB shot dead a junior high school teacher in Beoga, and Brimob personnel came under fire while evacuating residents by truck. Hundreds of residents fled to Ilaga after firefights (Tribratanews, detik, Tribun Papua).

23 Nov — Jakarta: The government designated the Papuan separatists an 'Armed Extremist Group' (KEB) in place of the 'KKB' label. Reports cite 172 people killed in attacks by the group in 2025–26 (ANTARA, iNews).

25 Nov — Asmat–Yahukimo waters: The TPNPB's Yahukimo command fired on two boats carrying 12 tonnes of rice to Dekai, wounding one person and leaving another missing, and the boats were reportedly burned. A joint team is searching for the victims (detik, ANTARA, Media Indonesia).
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Violence spread across Nduga, Puncak and the Yahukimo–Asmat supply routes. Relabelling the TPNPB as an 'Armed Extremist Group' signals a more militarised, counter-terrorism framing that makes dialogue less likely. Over the next 90 days, expect intensified TNI and police operations (Habema, Damai Cartenz) in Yahukimo, Nduga, Puncak, Intan Jaya and Pegunungan Bintang, with disputed casualty claims, detentions of indigenous Papuans and new waves of displacement. TPNPB attacks on teachers, health workers, road builders, aviation and supply logistics are likely to continue, with heightened risk around the 1 December anniversary. A single attack killing three or more people is a realistic possibility.

forecasts.statement: A single attack attributed to the TPNPB/OPM in Papua kills at least three people (civilians or security personnel, excluding attackers).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if, between 2026-11-27 and 2027-01-31, Reuters, AP, ANTARA, Kompas, Tempo or The Jakarta Post report one attack (one location, one day) in Papua attributed by police, the TNI or the TPNPB itself to the TPNPB/OPM that kills three or more people other than the attackers. Separate incidents may not be combined, and deaths of TPNPB fighters in security-force operations do not count.

countries.name: Thailand
incidents: 19–20 Nov — Narathiwat: In a coordinated overnight wave, suspected insurgents attacked CCTV cameras at multiple sites, continuing the pattern of sabotage against the security-camera network (Thai PBS World).
19–20 Nov — Bana, Mueang Pattani: Gunmen ambushed the mayor of Bana outside his home and wounded him (Bangkok Post).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. After the 13-site wave of 10–11 November, the insurgency returned to low-casualty sabotage and targeted shootings of local officials. Camera networks are a recurring target because they blind the security forces before larger operations. Over the next 90 days, expect sporadic IEDs, arson and ambushes in Narathiwat, Pattani, Yala and the Songkhla border districts, further attacks on officials and village defence volunteers, and security sweeps near the Malaysian border. Peace-dialogue contacts are unlikely to produce a ceasefire. Myanmar's fighting around Myawaddy may again send shells and refugees into Tak. A mass-casualty coordinated attack would warrant reassessment.

countries.name: Bangladesh
incidents: 20 Nov — Dhaka: Arsonists targeted the residence of Minister Humayun Kabir. The Business Standard counted four deaths and arson and bomb attacks in 21 districts over six days, and the government deployed 90 additional BGB platoons nationwide (Firstpost, TBS, Al Jazeera).

20–21 Nov — Narail: After the killing of two BNP leaders, more than 50 houses of Awami League supporters, including Hindu homes, were set on fire in reprisal, which sparked further clashes (India Today, Indian Express, Al Jazeera).

23–24 Nov — Dhaka: Blasts and arson hit the capital as the government vowed to arrest Hasina if she returns from India. On 24 Nov Hasina said she will return on 16 Dec (Victory Day) and asked for a Biman flight from Delhi (Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, NewsDrum).

24–26 Nov — Gazipur and Munshiganj: Police fired tear gas and sound grenades at garment workers blocking roads over a Tk 17,000 minimum-wage demand (Reuters, NDTV). An Awami League leader was shot dead on 25 Nov (IANS), and a BNP factional clash with gunfire and crude bombs killed one person in Munshiganj on 26 Nov (TBS).
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Hasina's 16 December return date gives the unrest a fixed countdown. The Awami League's crude-bomb and arson campaign continues, BNP supporters are answering with reprisal burnings such as Narail, and political killings and BNP factional clashes add to the toll. The government is responding with BGB deployments, mass arrests and a public arrest pledge, and is blaming India. Over the next 90 days, expect escalating hartal and lockdown calls around 16 December, bombings and vehicle arson in Dhaka and the Gopalganj–Faridpur–Narail belt, attacks on minorities caught in reprisals, and heavy-handed policing that risks deaths from police fire. A day with five or more deaths remains a realistic possibility. Hasina actually setting foot in Bangladesh by mid-January is unlikely, since it requires Indian facilitation and means arrest under a death sentence, but a staged attempt at the border or airport is possible. Garment-wage protests in Gazipur and Ashulia will recur.

forecasts.statement: Political violence linked to the Awami League protest campaign (clashes, bombings, arson or police fire) kills at least five people in Bangladesh on a single day.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, The Daily Star or Prothom Alo report, between 2026-11-20 and 2027-01-31, at least five deaths on one calendar day nationwide in clashes, attacks, arson or security-force fire connected to Awami League protests, lockdowns or Hasina's return, or to reprisals against them.

forecasts.statement: Sheikh Hasina physically enters Bangladesh (arriving by air or land, whether or not she is arrested on arrival).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC, The Daily Star or Prothom Alo report that Sheikh Hasina arrived on Bangladeshi territory (including an airport or land port, or in custody) between 2026-11-27 and 2027-01-15. Announcements, travel attempts stopped before entry, or video addresses do not count.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
incidents: 20 Nov — Ahungalla, Galle district: Police appealed for public help to arrest a shooting suspect (Daily Mirror).
25 Nov — Colombo: China signed an agreement to help modernise Sri Lanka Police, as Tamil groups raised complaints of police abuse (Newswire, Tamil Guardian).
26 Nov — Sri Lanka: A police officer wanted over the theft of a T-56 rifle was arrested in Dubai and returned to Sri Lanka (Ada Derana, The Morning).
countries.coa: LOW maintained. The security picture remains criminal. Underworld and narcotics-linked shootings continue, often involving former military personnel or stolen T-56 rifles, and the state is answering with an anti-drug drive, extraditions and police modernisation, now with Chinese support that Tamil groups view warily. Over the next 90 days, expect continued gang shootings in the Western, Southern and Eastern provinces and arrests linked to the anti-drug drive. Maaveerar commemorations in the North and East may bring friction with police but are unlikely to turn violent. No change in the overall threat picture is expected.

regions.name: Americas
overview: Haiti: the offensive against Viv Ansanm became the deadliest week of the intervention so far, and the intervening forces took their first losses. Haitian police, with the Vectus Global-run Task Force, say they killed 54 suspected gang members in Martissant on 19–20 November while trying to reopen National Road 2. The GSF reported six more killed at the Marassa Bridge (Tabarre) on 22 November. On 20 November an accidental explosion at a Salvadoran camp killed three Salvadoran soldiers, who according to Bukele were trying to dislodge a grenade from a drone; Bukele then said troops who want to go home may leave without reprisal. Gangs hit back against civilians: an armed group from Clemenceau killed at least 10 farmers at a market in Bongars (Kenscoff) on 25 November. The four Salvadoran technicians missing since 18 October are still unaccounted for.

Colombia: the bombing campaign has sped up to more than one strike a week, and attacks on the security forces continue. The government announced its 10th strike, 'Operation Neptuno' against the ELN in Dagua (Valle del Cauca), and its 11th, 'Operation Ninfa' against Mordisco's Front 44 in Mapiripan (Meta), each killing five, both made public on 21 November. Attacks on the security forces went on: an attack with improvised launch ramps on an army battalion in La Jagua de Ibirico (Cesar) on 22 November killed one soldier and wounded 12. An ambush in Padilla (Cauca) on 25 November killed two police officers and wounded four.

Ecuador and Peru: criminal violence is unchanged, and Ecuador votes under heavy security. Gunmen killed four people at a street family party in south-west Guayaquil on 22 November, one of two party shootings in the city that night, ahead of the 29 November local elections, which some 92,000 police and soldiers will guard. A NYT report on 24 November said Washington paused joint military operations with Ecuador by mid-October while it investigates a lethal September raid; Quito says the cooperation plan stands. In Peru, police arrested two 17-year-olds from 'La Nueva Hermandad' over the 17 November killing of a bus driver in Jicamarca, and gunmen shot dead a taxi driver in Villa El Salvador on 25 November.

Elsewhere, the pressure is socio-economic. In Venezuela, the PNB blocked a public-sector wage march to Miraflores on 24 November, with an unverified 5–10 workers hurt. On 25 November Machado spoke to about 3,000 students at the UCV unhindered, as she presses for a 2027 election date. In Bolivia, a 14.6% diesel price rise on 24 November triggered about 40 transport road blockades on 25 November; police used tear gas in Sucre and detained 16, and the COB has called a national march for 27 November. Cuba's generation deficit held around 1,700 MW, and independent unionist Emilio Gottardi was detained in Havana on 25 November. The Dominican Republic is deporting about 1,300 Haitians a day across a calm border. Jamaica's violence remains criminal and policing-related.

countries.name: Venezuela
incidents: 24 Nov — Caracas: Health, education and university unions marched from La Hoyada toward Miraflores over wages and Christmas bonuses, as part of a 24–48-hour national protest strike. Bolivarian National Police (PNB) cordons stopped the march near Avenida Baralt (Salas and Balconcito corners); marchers reported shoving, beatings and confiscated phones, and between five and ten workers hurt. The injury count comes from one left-wing outlet and is unverified.

25 Nov — Caracas (UCV Aula Magna): Maria Corina Machado addressed about 3,000 students at the Central University of Venezuela without hindrance. She promised a transition 'without revenge', called for presidential elections next year and presented her 'Liberal Democratic Republic' platform; she remains excluded from the government–opposition talks.

19–20 Nov — Caracas: The National Assembly's Judicial Nominations Committee closed the call for renewal of the Supreme Court (TSJ) with 1,343 applications; the candidate list was due on 20 November, followed by a 15-working-day objection period. This is the first concrete step on the talks' TSJ agenda item.

19 Nov — Miranda (Fuerte Guaicaipuro): The Venezuelan Prison Observatory said about 70 detainees at the Guaicaipuro military detention centre are held in roofless areas without electricity, exposed to sun and rain. Foro Penal's latest count remains 321 political prisoners, 140 of them military.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The contest is now mainly socio-economic and institutional. Public-sector unions held a 12-hour strike on 16 November and a 24–48-hour strike with a march on Miraflores on 24 November, which the PNB stopped with force but no reported deaths. The TSJ renewal process has formally started with 1,343 applicants, which gives the talks their first deliverable. Machado's unhindered UCV rally on 25 November shows the opposition's political space is wider than before, while she remains outside the negotiations and presses for a 2027 election date. In Apure there was no reported fighting following the FANB deployment, and the alleged 30 October strike on an ELN camp remains unconfirmed by Caracas. Over the next 90 days, expect the TSJ shortlist and appointments to move ahead, possibly followed by CNE changes, before any election date is fixed, plus further drip-feed prisoner releases. Expect also escalating union action over salaries and bonuses into December: 48–72-hour stoppages and more marches, met by police containment rather than mass arrests. Along the border, expect continued FANB pressure on ELN and dissident structures in coordination with Bogota and Washington; an armed ELN response that kills Venezuelan troops remains unlikely. Upgrade to HIGH if protests are dispersed with deaths, if Machado is detained, or if FANB–ELN fighting with casualties becomes recurrent.

forecasts.statement: Venezuela's interim government or the CNE officially announces a specific date for a presidential election.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP or EFE report that the Rodriguez government or the National Electoral Council has formally set a calendar date for a presidential election by 12 February 2027.

forecasts.statement: At least one member of Venezuela's armed forces (FANB) is killed in an armed clash with or attack by the ELN or FARC dissidents on Venezuelan territory.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, EFE, Efecto Cocuyo, El Pitazo or the FANB itself report that at least one Venezuelan soldier or National Guard member was killed by the ELN or a FARC dissident group inside Venezuela between 19 November 2026 and 15 February 2027.

countries.name: Colombia
incidents: 21 Nov — Dagua, Valle del Cauca (vereda La Elsa): President De la Espriella announced 'Operation Neptuno', an aerial bombing of the ELN's Luis Carlos Cardenas Arbelaez front (led by alias 'Berta') that killed five alleged members. He called it the 10th strategic bombing of his government; one EFE report places the strike earlier in the week.

21 Nov — Mapiripan, Meta: A pre-dawn bombing, 'Operation Ninfa', against Front 44 'Antonio Ricaurte' of Ivan Mordisco's FARC dissidents killed five alleged members, according to the President. Local media count it as the government's 11th bombing.

22 Nov — La Jagua de Ibirico, Cesar: An attack on an army battalion using improvised ramps to launch explosive devices killed one soldier and wounded 12. The army called it terrorism; both the ELN and the Clan del Golfo operate in the area, and no group has been officially identified.

25 Nov — Padilla, Cauca: Gunmen ambushed a police patrol escorting municipal officials to a park inauguration, killing patrolmen Kevin David Torres Berdugo and Bairon Jesus Riascos Murillo and wounding four. The Padilla police station was then harassed with gunfire. Some outlets blame FARC dissidents; responsibility has not been officially established.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The state's air campaign has accelerated to about one bombing a week. Two strikes made public on 21 November, against the ELN in Dagua and Mordisco's Front 44 in Mapiripan, each killed five, bringing the government's count to 11. The government says it has inflicted 357 'affectations' on the ELN, including 51 killed, between 7 August and 19 November. Armed groups keep striking back at the security forces, now with improvised launch ramps as well as drones: one soldier was killed and 12 wounded in La Jagua de Ibirico, and two police were killed in a Padilla ambush. Over the next 90 days, expect the 'for every attack, a bombing' policy to sustain this tempo across Catatumbo, Cauca, Valle, Meta, Antioquia and Arauca. Two of the four new bombings in the open forecast are already done, so that forecast now looks closer to highly likely. Expect continued drone, explosive and ambush attacks on bases, stations and patrols, and ELN–Front 33 fighting with civilian displacement in Catatumbo. A single attack killing five or more security-force members remains a realistic possibility. Civilian or minor casualties in a bombing are the main political risk for the campaign.

forecasts.statement: A single attack by an armed group in Colombia kills five or more soldiers and/or police officers.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, EFE or Colombian national media (El Tiempo, El Espectador) report one incident (one attack or ambush on one day) in which at least five members of the security forces were killed by an armed group, by 12 February 2027.

forecasts.statement: The Colombian government carries out at least four new aerial bombing operations against armed groups after 15 November 2026 (El Tiempo counted nine under President De la Espriella by that date).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the President, the Defence Ministry or the Military Forces announce or acknowledge at least four new aerial bombing operations conducted between 16 November 2026 and 15 February 2027, as reported by El Tiempo, El Espectador, Infobae or EFE.

countries.name: Haiti
incidents: 19–20 Nov — Martissant, Port-au-Prince: Haitian police units (SWAT, UTAG, UDMO), backed by the Task Force run by private contractor Vectus Global, armoured vehicles and explosive-laden drones, say they killed 54 suspected members of the Village de Dieu and Grand Ravine gangs (34 on 19 November, 20 on 20 November). The aim is to reopen National Road 2 to the south; police reported no losses and did not say what ground was retaken.

20 Nov — Salvadoran base, Haiti: An accidental explosion during an operation killed three Salvadoran soldiers, Lt Cristian Daniel Palacios Santos and Corporals Emerson Zepeda Zelada and Wilber Serrano Medina, and injured a fourth. Bukele said the corporals were trying to dislodge a grenade from a drone. He announced a $1 million fund for the families and said troops who want to leave Haiti may do so without reprisal.

22 Nov — Marassa Bridge, Tabarre and Gros-Morne, Artibonite: The GSF said its troops killed six suspected gang members and seized five firearms at the Marassa Bridge. It also killed one in Boston (Cite Soleil) and met armed resistance in Gros-Morne, where a magistrate reported three bodies of suspected Kokorat San Ras members.

25 Nov — Bongars, Kenscoff: Around 04:00, armed men from the Clemenceau area attacked an informal market with firearms and machetes, killing at least 10 farmers and wounding seven (Le Nouvelliste via EFE). Police launched a helicopter-supported pursuit.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The offensive has broadened from Salvadoran strikes on 400 Mawozo and Taliban leaders to a multi-force campaign. The PNH and the contractor-run Task Force are pushing into Martissant to reopen the southern road, while the GSF fights in Tabarre, Cite Soleil and the Artibonite. Police alone claim 54 killed in two days, with no independent verification. The first Salvadoran deaths came on 20 November, in an accident rather than enemy action. Bukele's offer to let troops leave freely, plus Security Minister Villatoro's line that El Salvador withdraws once the four missing technicians are found, makes the length of the Salvadoran presence the main strategic uncertainty. Gangs are answering with massacres of civilians outside the core battle zones, such as the market in Bongars, Kenscoff. Over the next 90 days, expect continued high-casualty police and Task Force operations along National Road 2 and in the Cul-de-Sac. Expect also gang reprisals against civilians in Kenscoff, the Artibonite and the eastern communes, more displacement, and growing UN and NGO scrutiny of the unverified death tolls and contractor use of explosive drones. The capture or death of a top-tier leader remains a realistic possibility. A drawdown of Salvadoran troops before the missing technicians are found is unlikely but would weaken the campaign. Watch whether the electoral calendar slips.

events.place: Marassa Bridge, Tabarre and Gros-Morne, Artibonite

forecasts.statement: 400 Mawozo leader Wilson Joseph ('Lanmo Sanjou') is killed or taken into custody.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Haitian authorities, the Salvadoran government or the GSF confirm Joseph's death, capture or surrender, as reported by AP, Reuters, the Miami Herald or the Haitian Times, by 12 February 2027.

forecasts.statement: Haitian or Salvadoran authorities confirm the fate (found alive or confirmed dead) of the four Salvadoran aviation technicians missing since 18 October.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the Salvadoran or Haitian government officially states that the four technicians have been recovered alive or that their deaths are confirmed (identified remains included), as reported by AP, Reuters or Al Jazeera, by 31 January 2027.

forecasts.statement: Taliban gang leader Jeff Larose ('Jeff Canaan') is killed or taken into custody.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Haitian authorities, the Salvadoran government or the GSF confirm Larose's death, capture or surrender, as reported by AP, Reuters, the Miami Herald or the Haitian Times, by 15 February 2027.

countries.name: Cuba
incidents: 21–23 Nov — Nationwide: The Electric Union (UNE) reported outages lasting all day on 21 November and into the early hours of 22 November. It forecast cuts of 1,713 MW at peak on 22 November and 1,725 MW on 23 November, with only about 1,105 MW available against 2,800 MW of demand.

25 Nov — Havana: The Independent Trade Union Association of Cuba (ASIC) reported that State Security detained independent unionist Emilio Gottardi Gottardi as he left his home; his whereabouts were unknown.

22 Nov — El Cobre, Santiago de Cuba: Food-aid organiser Yoel Alejandro Perez Serrano reached 15 days in detention without charges, according to former political prisoner Jose Daniel Ferrer; his arrest had triggered street protests in El Cobre. The Cuban Observatory of Human Rights recorded 3,438 repressive actions from January to October 2026.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. The power deficit eased slightly from about 1,850 MW to about 1,700 MW, but all-day outages continue, the grid has collapsed completely six times in 2026 (most recently on 4 November), and water supply fails wherever pumping depends on the grid. Repression stays targeted: incommunicado detention of a unionist in Havana, and a food-aid activist in El Cobre held for over two weeks without charges. No new mass protest was reported this week, but the Calabazar barricades on 13 November show how quickly local anger turns into road-blocking. Over the next 90 days, expect continued deficits above 1,500 MW and at least one further total grid disconnection, which remains likely. Expect also recurring pot-banging and barricade protests in outer Havana and the east, met by short detentions, Decree-Law 370 fines and local internet cuts, and continued detention of independent unionists and activists. Upgrade to CRITICAL only if protests coordinate across several cities, security forces use lethal force, or state control visibly erodes.

forecasts.statement: Cuba's national electric system (SEN) suffers a total nationwide disconnection (complete grid collapse).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the Ministry of Energy and Mines or the UNE announces a total disconnection of the SEN, as reported by EFE, Reuters, AP or 14ymedio, by 12 February 2027. Partial or regional collapses do not count.

countries.name: Ecuador
incidents: 22 Nov — Guayaquil (Abel Castillo and Modesto Chavez Franco, south-west): Gunmen opened fire on a family party in the street at about 19:15, killing four people, reportedly with no criminal records, and wounding three. Police gave no motive.
22 Nov — Guayaquil (Calle 44 and El Oro): A separate attack on a children's party the same night killed an 18-year-old and wounded two minors, including a two-month-old baby.

24–25 Nov — Quito/Washington: The New York Times reported that the Trump administration had paused joint military operations with Ecuador by mid-October while investigating possible abuses in a 23 September Ecuadorian raid that killed gang figure Carlos German Munoz Jara. Interior Minister Reimberg said on 25 November that a joint work plan remains and that US aircraft and helicopters are still in the country.

Ongoing (to 29 Nov) — Nationwide: Authorities are deploying 57,470 police and 34,768 soldiers to secure the 29 November local elections, under the Decree 532 state of exception in eight provinces. The campaign closed on 26 November, two weeks after Huaquillas mayoral candidate Ronald Farfan and council candidate Cristhian Rugel were killed.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Guayaquil again saw multiple-victim party shootings on 22 November, and 2026 has already passed 190 massacres. Homicides are down about 11% year on year, but organised violence by Los Lobos, Los Choneros and their splinters still meets the CRITICAL threshold. A new strategic factor is the reported US pause in joint operations, triggered by a rights investigation into the September raid. If it persists, it removes part of the intelligence and air support behind Noboa's 'internal armed conflict' strategy, although Quito insists the cooperation plan stands. Over the next 90 days, the 29 November vote and the handover of local offices are the near-term risk: attacks on newly elected or defeated local officials, especially in El Oro, Manabi, Guayas and Los Rios, are plausible. After the vote, expect renewal of the state of exception around 13 December, continued military-police sweeps, prison violence, and a fifth curfew if killings spike, which remains likely. A public resumption of joint US–Ecuador operations by late February is a realistic possibility, depending on the outcome of the US investigation.

forecasts.statement: President Noboa decrees a fifth curfew of 2026–27 covering at least one coastal province (Guayas, Manabi, Los Rios, El Oro or Esmeraldas).
forecasts.resolution: Yes if an executive decree imposing a new night-time curfew in at least one of these provinces takes effect after 12 November 2026, as reported by Primicias, El Universo, EFE or Reuters, by 12 February 2027.

forecasts.statement: The United States and/or Ecuador publicly confirm that joint US–Ecuador military operations against criminal groups, reported paused by the New York Times on 24 November 2026, have resumed.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if the Pentagon, SOUTHCOM, the US State Department or the Ecuadorian government states that joint operations have resumed, or Reuters, AP or the NYT report their resumption, by 26 February 2027. Statements that a 'work plan' merely exists do not count.

countries.name: Peru
incidents: 19 Nov — Callao: Dirincri police arrested two 17-year-olds over the 17 November killing of El Mandarino bus driver Jose Miranda Torres in Jicamarca. Police link them to the 'La Nueva Hermandad' gang, investigated for contract killing and extortion; six more adults and minors are named as suspects.

25 Nov — Villa El Salvador (Lima): Two gunmen on a motorcycle intercepted a ride-hailing taxi at the junction of Avenida Separadora Industrial and Avenida Jose Carlos Mariategui, near a Metro Line 1 station, and fired up to ten shots, killing the driver. No arrests were reported. RPP counts 64 urban transport drivers killed in 2026.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Gangs keep killing transport workers in Lima: after the Jicamarca bus driver on 17 November came a taxi driver in Villa El Salvador on 25 November, and RPP counts 64 urban drivers killed this year. The quick arrest of two teenage hitmen from 'La Nueva Hermandad' shows how gangs use minors and does nothing to change the extortion economy. The state retains territorial control under the Lima/Callao state of emergency to 26 December, and the cargo hauliers' diesel strike of 16–18 November, which included clashes and detentions in Huanuco, is suspended but unresolved. Over the next 90 days, expect continued killings of drivers and mototaxi riders, company stoppages after each killing, and renewal of the emergency in late December. A widespread Lima/Callao transport strike remains likely if killings continue over the holiday period, as does renewed cargo blockades if fuel prices rise again. Upgrade triggers: a mass-casualty attack on a bus, attacks on officials, or deadly clashes during strikes.

forecasts.statement: Public transport unions in Lima/Callao carry out a strike (paro) against extortion in which a majority of formal bus companies suspend service for at least one day.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Peruvian national media (El Comercio, La Republica, RPP, Infobae Peru) or Reuters/AP report a transport strike in Lima/Callao described as widespread or as paralysing most routes, held after 12 November 2026 and by 12 February 2027.

countries.name: Bolivia
incidents: 24 Nov — National: The government raised the price of diesel by 14.6%, from Bs 17.95 to Bs 20.57 a litre, the third increase of 2026, as part of phasing out subsidies under an IMF agreement. President Paz said prices must track international levels. Transport unions declared themselves in emergency, and the Cochabamba Civic Committee denounced a 'dieselazo'.

25 Nov — Sucre, Oruro, Potosi, La Paz: About 40 road blockades were recorded on the first day of a two-day transport strike. Police used tear gas to clear roads in Sucre and detained at least 16 transport workers in Chuquisaca; a highway was blocked in Oruro and there were partial stoppages in Potosi and La Paz.

25 Nov — La Paz: Miners, teachers and factory workers instructed their members to join a national COB march against the diesel hike called for Friday 27 November. Oruro heavy-transport operators proposed an indefinite national strike.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The flashpoint has shifted from the Chapare to the economy. The 24 November diesel rise brought transport unions, the COB, miners, teachers and the Cochabamba civic movement into a common front, with about 40 blockades on the first strike day and tear gas and arrests in Sucre. The state of exception in force since June formally restricts road closures and is due for renewal around 17 December. In the Tropico, Morales loyalists still hold the El Castillo checkpoint, and the 'armed uprising' case and migration alert stand, but there was no new clash. Over the next 90 days, expect the 27 November COB march and further rolling transport strikes. A multi-day national blockade is a realistic possibility if the government does not offer compensation such as freight-rate or transport-fare concessions, although an outright reversal of the hike is unlikely given the IMF programme. Expect also renewal of the state of exception and continued friction around anti-drug operations in the Chapare. Upgrade to HIGH if blockades of main highways last several days with deaths, if security forces and protesters clash lethally, or if an operation to arrest Morales meets armed resistance.

forecasts.statement: Bolivian police or armed forces launch an operation inside the Tropico de Cochabamba (Chapare) aimed at arresting Evo Morales.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if Reuters, AP, EFE or Bolivian national media (El Deber, Los Tiempos, Pagina Siete) report that security forces moved into the Chapare in an attempt to execute an arrest warrant against Morales, whether or not the arrest succeeds, by 15 February 2027.

forecasts.statement: The Bolivian government reverses or suspends the 24 November 2026 diesel price increase, restoring a pump price below Bs 20.57 per litre.
forecasts.resolution: Yes if a supreme decree or official government/YPFB announcement lowers the regulated diesel price below Bs 20.57 per litre or suspends the increase, as reported by EFE, Reuters, El Deber, Los Tiempos or Unitel, by 31 January 2027. Targeted subsidies or compensation for specific sectors without a lower pump price do not count.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
incidents: 23 Nov — Dajabon, Elias Pina, Jimani, Pedernales: The Migration Directorate (DGM), supported by the armed forces and police, reported 1,298 detentions and 1,317 deportations to Haiti in one day, with Dajabon recording the most detentions (286). The pace of about 10,000 deportations a week since early November continues.

23 Nov — Santo Domingo: The Duartian Institute warned about the Haitian crisis and called for reinforced border surveillance and continued deportations through Christmas. The government maintains the frontier is calm despite gang tension in Haiti.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Border crossings operate under about 11,000 troops, with special forces, armour and drones, and the state is deporting about 1,300 Haitians a day without reported incidents. Over the next 90 days, the main external risks are the intensifying operations in Haiti (Martissant, the Cul-de-Sac, Kenscoff) and gang massacres east of Port-au-Prince. These could push displaced civilians or fleeing gang members toward Jimani and Belladere. Santo Domingo's declared support to El Salvador could also make Dominican interests a target for Viv Ansanm. Expect continued reinforcement, fence construction, deportations at roughly the current pace, and possible temporary crossing closures if fighting moves toward the frontier. Upgrade to MODERATE if gang violence crosses the border, Dominican forces engage armed groups, or cross-border incidents cause casualties.

countries.name: Jamaica
incidents: 23 Nov — Knockpatrick, Manchester: The mother of Kymani Bindloss, shot dead by police on 2 November in what police called a confrontation, publicly disputed the police account of her son as a murder suspect. An alleged eyewitness says he raised his hands before being shot. The Gleaner says at least 256 people have been killed by the security forces this year.

24 Nov — Sligoville, St Catherine: Ayasus Lawrence, 26, shot nine times during a police-military operation the previous week, was charged with possession of a prohibited weapon, unauthorised possession of ammunition and larceny. His father says he was shot in the back while fleeing.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Murder figures continue at historic lows: the third quarter of 2026 had the fewest murders in more than 30 years, and St Catherine and St Thomas report sharp declines. The dominant security issue is the security forces' own use of lethal force: at least 256 people have been killed by the security forces this year, and families increasingly dispute police accounts of 'confrontations', as in the Bindloss and Sligoville cases. Over the next 90 days, expect further contested police shootings and INDECOM probes, occasional roadblock protests after disputed killings, and the usual December rise in criminal violence. Upgrade to MODERATE only if planned ambushes on police, sustained unrest in Kingston, St Andrew or St Catherine, or a sharp rise in gang feuds emerges.
